label: static-inference
claim: The X-M1 1.50 boot records, loaders and decoded images target an ARMv7-R core with a PMSAv7 MPU and VFPv3-D16, matching Cortex-R4F: code programs PMSA MPU region registers (c6,c2,0 then c6,c1,{4,0,2}), never accesses TTBR0/TTBR1/TTBCR or DACR, writes Cortex-R4/R5 implementation-defined c15,c5,0 and c9,c1,1, uses ARMv7 DSB/ISB and cache-ID registers, saves only d0-d15 in the VFP context switch, uses ARMv6T2 MOVW/MOVT throughout and contains no A32 SDIV/UDIV. The native runner now emulates Unicorn 2.1.4 Cortex-R5F, the closest available model, and rejects R5F-only A32 divide.
scope: Static inference, 2026-10-03, from permissive whole-image LLVM A32 linear-sweep listings of the exact 1.50 boot records (payload 0x40048/0x50048), loaders (0x40000/0xd0000), plain image (0x01100000) and decoded id4/id5, with the cited sequences read in context. Emulator model properties read from Unicorn 2.1.4 source. Independently reviewed and corrections verified (CPU-REVIEW-01).
sources: Sibling lead only: https://github.com/tiredboffin/fffw/wiki/EXR-II-CPU; FujiHack wiki https://wiki.fujihack.org/todo/ (unsourced ARM11 note, other bodies)
commands: devenv shell -- llvm-objcopy -I binary -O elf32-littlearm --rename-section .data=.text,alloc,load,code,contents IMAGE.bin IMAGE.elf

claim: In the X-M1 1.50 images the error words of D0 opcode 0x00200001 are the reply fields 0x014698a0 and 0x014698a4, and handler 0x00d803cc writes them at exactly four sites: 0x00d805b8 stores (9,3) for a function above 5 from the test at 0x00d80450, for a length outside 1 to 256 from the test at 0x00d8045c, and for callback status 3; 0x00d805d4 stores (1,0xffff) for status 2; 0x00d8059c stores (1,3) for status 4 and for nothing else; 0x00d805f0 sets transfer byte 0x01469cc0 for status 1. The arms are selected by the table at 0x00d8058c-0x00d80598 indexed by status minus 1 from the ldrls pc at 0x00d80584, and any other status leaves the words at the zeros written by the dispatcher clearing loop 0x00d80ac4, which is the (0,0) acceptance. claim: On X-M1 1.50 the ordinary boot accepts the stored settings or rebuilds defaults through one gate. The boot gate 0x0073e0b0 -> 0x0073cbfc -> 0x006a75a4 opens area 2 as 0x200-byte records, count 0x3e, in logical blocks 0x3d6/0x3d7 and accepts only when the log read returns 0, byte 0x409c29c6 is 0xaa and byte 0x409c29c7 negates the sum of 0x409c29b8..0x409c29c6. Failure runs 0x006a6fd8(0) and sets 0x0089f834, after which 0x006a8abc defaults and commits the custom record in area 3, blocks 0x3d8/0x3d9. The resetting boot repairs the custom record (0x006a86c4 commits it) and the retained header (0x006a6ddc writes it) itself, while area 2 is written only by 0x006a8074, whose two firmware callers are the queue-2 lifecycle callbacks 0x00ec2cb8 and 0x00ec4154, so only an orderly power-off rewrites it. 0x006a6ddc writes the header as sixteen independent byte transactions with the checksum byte last. The maintenance power-off path 0x0063975c skips the area-2 save by routing, writes no settings store and reaches none in a walk of 890 functions; the defaults write cycle D measured at a POWER-switch jig ending runs outside 0x0063975c, through the queue-2 0x504 bridge (E-ENDING-RESET-CALLER-150). Retained-header bytes 6, 10 and 11, which differ between POWER-switch and supply-cut jig endings, do not gate this acceptance. The only writer of header byte 6 bit 0 is property 0x282, whose case body 0x6300e0 edits settings-image byte 6 at 0x630124/0x630128, mirrors it to 0x0089ec06 and pushes all 16 bytes at 0x63012c; its only entry 0x00643a08 is called with 1 from the sync site 0x63763c and with 0 from image-5 0x00ca41e4, the branch that runs only when 0xc021f4 returned -1. The boot action 0x0073cbfc reads byte 6 through 0x6a6e68 at 0x73cc74, tests bit 0 at 0x73cc78 and acts only on the set state, calling 0x726c74(1,0xf0) at 0x73cc90 and posting the image-5 debug event 0xd3bc34(5) at 0x73cc94-0x73cca8; a completed maintenance boot sets the bit itself, so the clear state marks the orderly terminal branch. Byte 11 bits 0-3 are written by the case bodies of property ids 2, 1, 3 and 175 at 0x62fee4, 0x62ff60, 0x62ffe0 and 0x630060; the boot record's 0x0001386c tests for low nibble 7 at 0x1388c-0x13898, and its only caller 0x00011d58 folds the result into 0x400a0144 at 0x11f00-0x11f18 through 0x13b80, which ignores that argument and returns 0 on every path (r0 overwritten at 0x13b98, the 1024-length branch bhs 0x13be8, mov r0, #0 at 0x13c10), so 0x400a0144 is 0 in every boot and the test has no effect; 0x400a0140 and 0x400a0144 read 0 in the three captured maintenance boots examined (hardware-observed). No case body writes byte 10, so a stored 0x00 there comes from a wholesale 16-byte write such as the 0x006a6fd8 template push; the byte-10 setter 0x6a7de0 (called at image-5 0xf3af7c and 0xf3af88) and getter 0x6a7e68 (called at 0xf3be00) mirror a two-state field of the block at 0x016c0714 (state 3 clears, state 4 sets). Cycle D found the store already defaulted before the ordinary boot read it (E-JIG-CYCLE-D-150), so the settings loss after a POWER-switch jig ending does not depend on this failure branch running.
scope: X-M1 firmware 1.50 decoded images 4, 5 and 6, both loaders and both boot records: ordinary-boot settings acceptance, retained-header readers and writers, and flash log areas 2 and 3. Host-only static analysis; the header cell values quoted are read from the cycle A, B and C jig captures of E-JIG-CYCLE-D-150.

label: static-inference
claim: On X-M1 1.50 the boot records load neither image 5 nor the plain image. Boot record 1 looks up segment-table ids 0, 1 and 4 only (0x1d18 mov r0,#0, 0x1d24 mov r0,#1, 0x225c mov r0,#4, each bl 0x4174), copying ids 0/1 with the 128 KiB block reader 0x231c and decompressing id 4 through the shared streaming loader (0x3d3c setup; engine helpers 0x3c54/0x3cbc/0x3ce4/0x3d08); neither loader image calls into the boot block (no BL target in 0x0000-0x3fff) and boot record 2 calls none of its own helper copies. Image 4 loads both, from its flashloader task 0x73b3a0 (created by 0x73ac7c, mailbox 0x3c): case 0 at 0x73b4ac calls 0x6a96c0, which takes segment-table id 5 (entry at payload 0x14013c: load 0x00bf1a00, size 0x4f1e60, flash 0x002c0000/0x002e0000), reads logical blocks 0x16-0x2c into staging 0x43e40000 and feeds the 0xfff43000 engine, delivering 0x00bf1a00; case 3 at 0x73b554 calls 0x6a9844, which takes id 6 (entry at payload 0x140160: flash 0x005a0000/0x00360000) and reads blocks 0x2d-0x47 straight to the destination word at 0x61c1a8 = 0x01100000 with no engine and no CPU copy loop. Image 4 also carries a relocated engine driver (0x6843c8, 0x684308, wrappers 0x684760/0x6847d8/0x684828/0x684880) that forms the register addresses with movw/movt pairs, which the earlier literal-only scan missed.
scope: X-M1 1.50 decoded image 4 plus the preserved payload segment table and record headers; host-only, spot-checked from the bytes at every named address on 2026-10-07; the installed body shows both images resident (E-RAM-PROBE-150)
limitations: Static inference: no load was observed in progress, and the task and command sequence is read from the image, not executed.
The companion core's part in any of the loads is not assigned.

Entry 6's load, size and bss words are dead in this build: 0x6a9844 is its only reader and uses only the flash fields and the extent descriptor, and the loader stages never call the entry getter; why the vendor table repeats entry 5's values is not derivable from the images.

The staging constants are hard-coded per caller (boot 0x42e40000, id-5 loader 0x43e40000), image 4, 5 and 6 code uses 0x42e40000 elsewhere, and no code derives either constant, so the choice is not explained by the images.
The queue producers that post the command words behind cases 0 and 3 are not traced to a UI action.

claim: Loader A's log writer 0x42188 appends 0x10-byte entries to a fixed store at 0x400a0800, under a header whose capacity halfword is 0x1ffc at +0x1c and whose next-index halfword at +0x1e wraps to zero at capacity. The initializer writes 0x1ffc at 0x41458/0x4145c, clears entries to r4+0x1FFC0 at 0x41484-0x414a8 and hands 0x1fff4 bytes to the dump path at 0x423d4, so the store is 0x1fff4 bytes (0x400a0800-0x400c07f3, 8188 entries) and it sets the same layout for a second store at 0x40063460. Entries from +0x34 hold {type byte 0x72 on this path, thread byte = low byte of TPIDRURW or zero when its sign bit is set (0x421fc-0x42220), delta = [0xFFF91004] - [0xFFF91000] (0x42224-0x42234), tick = *(0x400c0800) (0x42238-0x42244), and one eight-character string prefix, whose two words land at +0x3c and +0x40 (0x42248-0x42254) from a single NUL-terminated r0 argument copied up to eight characters (0x42194-0x421b0)}. The writer body is gated on *(0x4004f25c) == 1 (0x421d0-0x421e0). The id-5 loader 0x6a96c0 calls it at 0x6a96f0 (MAIN_S) and 0x6a9834 (MAIN_E) unconditionally and at 0x6a9764/0x6a97a8/0x6a97b4/0x6a97c4 (LMAIN_S, LMAIN_E, DMAIN_S, DMAIN_E) behind the 0x6a9758 branch on 0x657184, so a read of the store after boot carries MAIN_S and MAIN_E in the tick words if the ring has not wrapped. read-log reads the store whole, 8188 slots in 512 windows, plus the tick cell at 0x400c0800 read twice in a row before the store and once after it; the first store window holds both header halfwords. Reads of the store confirmed the header and capacity, found the writer gate set in maintenance boots (E-LOG-READ3-150) and in an ordinary boot (E-CONSOLE-CONTROLS-PRE-REPAIR-150), and showed that each boot rewrites the store (E-LOG-PERSIST-150).

label: static-inference
claim: Host static closure of the X-M1 1.50 area-2 mutation set. Through the log layer, area 2 is mutated only by 0x006a8074 (direct callers 0x00ec2cb8 with argument 1 and 0x00ec4154 with argument 0), the area-2 whole-log erase wrapper 0x006a83d8, which has no caller and no reference of any form, and service dispatcher 0x00dbcaa4 cases 2 and 3 calling 0x006ab1e0; no computed, encoded, table or indirect reference to the seven area-2 mutation entries exists in the seven pinned artifacts (image 4, image 5, plain image, both loaders, both boot records) under the scanners' stated coverage. The twenty descriptor rows at 0x007c8cc0 partition map-relative device indices 0x00..0x7f disjointly, so encoded blocks 0x3d6/0x3d7, device indices 0x56/0x57, are uniquely area 2 and static descriptor overlap or duplicate logical mapping cannot reach them. Two conditional native paths sit below the descriptor layer: the lens-descriptor journal pair path 0x006bffc4 -> 0x006ac268/0x006ac198 erases and reprograms both area-2 banks when the journal tail byte is 0x2b, which needs a 0x2b in a block-0x28 link position that the tail copy can reach (the captured link positions read 0x33/0x34/0x2e with head 12, tail 0, count 13, so the static 0xff-or-<=0x14 bound is refuted by the captures) plus a journal-update step (0x7401 from the End Setting persistence step 0x00ec2d18 or the firmware-update commit step 0x00ec4618, 0x7403 from the image-5 step 0x00dc56b0 -> 0x006a0084 -> 0x006c14f4), no queue-2 post or journal trigger was found in the physical POWER/OFF chain's depth-bounded immediate-branch scan or in its resolved register-indirect edge (0x72b680 -> *(0x00829a0c) -> 0x72b210, which posts to queue 1 or 7); a full switch-path exclusion and a whole-cycle exclusion are both unproved, with the step selection unbound; the multi-block program entry 0x006a8de0 has ten call sites in six wrappers; the journal pair wrapper 0x006ac198 names 0x56/0x57 at k = 0x2b, and the rows-2/3 wrappers 0x006abfb4/0x006a9c70 can name them arithmetically because their offset-plus-length guard is a wrapping 32-bit add with no carry check (first-block index 0x29 + (off >> 17)), while no traced caller can close that gap: every traced offset is a small constant (0x237, 0x400000, 0x76800, 0x11c840, 0x2bb8e0, 0x3b4940, 0x3b8ba8, 0x3c31b0) and the parameter-derived lengths are sums of two quantities that each arrive shifted right by 3 (0x69f9b4/0x69fa40 add r2,r6,r2,lsr #3 after lsr r6,r6,#3 at 0x69f9ec-0x69f9f4), so each summand is at most 0x1fffffff and the length at most 0x3ffffffe, and off + len cannot reach 2^32, so no traced input names 0x56/0x57; that reach is nominal arithmetic reach, before the native operation's success checks; the raw device-block family can name raw blocks 0x3d6/0x3d7 only through service or update flows. Native read, program and erase success paths join completion before returning and queue no deferred media work, and the bounded-timeout abandon paths require an issued write or erase.
scope: Host-only static analysis of the pinned 1.50 artifacts and the descriptor table at 0x007c8cc0; the descriptor-layer and native-entry claims are scoped to the seven decoded artifacts
limitations: Code outside the seven decoded artifacts is unsearched; an out-of-artifact caller of the area-2 erase or append primitives remains unproved.

The rows-2/3 multi-block wrappers 0x006abfb4 and 0x006a9c70 guard with a wrapping 32-bit len + off sum without a carry check and index as 0x29 + (off >> 17), so nominal arithmetic reach to device indices outside the row, including 0x56/0x57, holds for callers outside the traced set, and even such a caller must still pass the native operation's success checks before any media write. No traced caller reaches the banks: the traced offsets are small constants and the parameter-derived lengths arrive as sums of two quantities that each shift right by 3 at 0x69f9b4/0x69fa40, so each summand is at most 0x1fffffff, the length at most 0x3ffffffe and off + len cannot reach 2^32. The two record-driven wrappers 0x0072b69c/0x0072b6c4 have no in-artifact caller.

The row-13 wrappers 0x006ab894/0x006ab9d4 index from base 0x5e and the row-17 site 0x006abbac from 0x6c, so those three cannot name 0x56/0x57 for any input, but their full-domain index sets reach 0x5e..0x805d and 0x6c..0x806b under the same wrapping guard.
Storage-controller microcode and electrical rail sequencing are unobserved; autonomous controller behavior is unproved, not supported.

Journal-pair trigger residuals are narrowed to the event cell: event code 0x015c1e84 is written only by the queue-2 receive 0x725318 at 0xec2688-0xec2698, the queue-2 posters are enumerated, and no queue-2 post or journal trigger was found in the POWER/OFF chain's depth-bounded immediate-branch scan (16 levels; no fixed point, no register-indirect resolution, edges attributed to the nearest preceding push-with-lr) or in its resolved indirect edges. Three of the 44 register-indirect sites in that closure resolve: the log layer's two lower-object callbacks, +0x30/+0x34 and +0x28/+0x2c, which are 0x006a6c54 and 0x006a6c04 for the area-2 object (the slot 0x0089f8f0 there is only a readiness flag, tested at 0x6ad310-0x6ad324 and set at 0x6ad09c-0x6ad0a0), and 0x72b680 loading slot 0x00829a0c after the installer at 0x72b6f4-0x72b704 writes 0x0072b210 there, which posts to queue 1 or 7 at 0x72b2ec through 0x72503c, so the application-event fanout remains an unclosed asynchronous route. label: static-inference
claim: The C0 open reply's bytes 4-7 are a fixed little-endian 0x00010000 (65536) and bytes 2-3 a zero halfword, written unconditionally by the C0 handler 0x00d7f56c in image 5: the handler prepares the reply at 0x0146989c, writes the SID there through the little-endian 16-bit helper 0xd7f364, then does `add r0, r4, #4; mov r1, #65536; bl 0xd7f384`, where 0xd7f384 stores its argument as four bytes low-first. Every captured open reply carries that tail, varying only in the SID: S02 and S03 on installed 1.00 and all eleven 1.50 sessions. No D1 length depends on the field: D1 at 0x00d7f8a4 checks the active session, the matching SID and a nonzero requested length, then stores that length at 0x01469868 without comparing the C0 field; bulk source 0x00d7efd4 supplies the unsigned minimum of requested and available length at 0x0146986c; config function 2 at 0x00d801cc prepares available length 292 at 0x00d80334-0x00d80338 with data at reply+36; and the pinned upstream config client requests payload+36 independently of max_pkt_size. A read window is therefore 256 adjustment bytes in an exact 292-byte D1 reply. The sibling host fujihack names the C0 field a maximum size; no mapped X-M1 artifact reads it back, and the D0 command handler's own length cap is 512, a different field, so the field's units stay unnamed. The transport's identify and end-setting paths require the exact little-endian constant, and the end-setting test carries a byte-swapped tail that only the little-endian parse refuses.

label: static-inference
claim: The tick cell 0x400c0800 is ordinary RAM in the log store's region and loader A manages it in three places, mirrored by the 0xd0000 loader. Its initializer 0x40b5c stores zero into the cell and registers the increment function 0x40b24 as callback id 32 through 0x4d8fc in every copy; 0x40b24 calls the selector at [0x4004dae0+0x104] and discards its result, then calls 0x427b8, and only when that returns zero does the callback load the cell, add one and store it, so one core maintains the tick. The block 0x40bb0-0x40c44 runs when the initializer's 0x427b8 check returned zero: it computes [0xFFF91000] with the reciprocal-multiply division by 1875 (magic 0x45E7B273, shift 9), stores the quotient into the cell, forms the remainder with mls against 1875, scales it by 30000 and stores 30000 minus 16 times the remainder into [0xFFF91004], zeroes then writes the control word at [0xFFF91008], and overwrites [0xFFF91004] with 30000, sixteen times 1875, which is the code's own statement of the division and means the phase value does not survive; 0x40c48-0x40c4c then starts 0x41108 with argument 32 on both paths. The loader initializers at 0x4089c/0xd089c publish the cell's address into interface slot +0x174 rather than writing the cell, twelve sites per loader load it (the log writers), image 4 loads it once at 0x00728784, and image 5 conditionally zeroes it at 0x00ec7d80 behind 0x69f8fc with 0x525a. So the tick is the 0xFFF91000 counter divided by 1875, its unit follows that counter's rate rather than a hardware latch, and a debug read of the cell copies bytes without side effects. This corrects the earlier reading of the 0x4089c store as the cell's initializer.

limitations: The 0xFFF91000 counter is unnamed. The tick rate measured 99.9 Hz on this body (E-AUTOACT-UNIT-150), which with the division by 1875 puts the counter near 187 kHz (static-inference).

The selector called at 0x40b38 runs first and its result is discarded, so only 0x427b8's return decides which copy increments; that the predicate distinguishes the cores comes from the repo's loader notes rather than from this disassembly.
The image-5 zeroing path at 0x00ec7d80 is conditional on 0x69f8fc with 0x525a and the meaning of that selector is unproved.

label: hardware-observed
claim: Two reviewed probe-bootrom sessions on XM1-body-01 running official 1.50 settle what lies past the 16 KiB boot-ROM block: 20261008T035458Z-probe-bootrom (66 windows: the 64-window lead range, 0x80004000 and 0x00000000) and 20261008T050828Z-probe-bootrom (130 windows: the lead range, the full 0x80004000-0x80007fff block, 0x80008000 and 0x00000000). Each completed with every window matching its journal hash, both gate readbacks holding (adjustment index 0xf7 = 1 after the enable write and 0 after the restore) and one completion record, and both reproduce the fffw bootrom digest over the lead windows (SHA-1 bed698ed1d91b5c29ce7c5d650156e6100c32cce, JASM_A_1 footer intact) first captured in E-BOOTROM-PROBE-150. The unique boot-ROM content is the 16 KiB block: all 64 windows of 0x80004000-0x80007fff are byte-identical to their 0x80000000-0x80003fff counterparts, the JASM_A_1 footer repeats at 0x80007ff0, and the windows at 0x80008000 and, in E-STRAP-READ-150, at 0x80010000 and 0x80100000 equal the block's first 256 bytes (SHA-256 ce27e3d02a39e1ed362923b40ddbba32e6b20d71a8cd509828901ba95e2192b3). Reads up to 1 MiB above the base therefore return the same block, a zeros-or-open-bus bound at 0x80008000 and a larger repeated image are refuted, and a second core instance is a weak reading because every sampled base returns identical content. The reset ldm's 32-byte fetch from 0x80003ff8 is a boundary-straddling over-read rather than a data structure: eight zero bytes after the JASM_A_1 footer plus 24 bytes of the repeated vector table, of which only the first word survives the zero-fill at 0x80000110. The window at 0x00000000 holds the running firmware's exception vector area in low RAM, not ROM: eight ldr pc,[pc,#0x18] vectors whose target words are 0x00001800, 0x00040100, 0x000401b4, 0x0061c73c, 0x0061c7f0, 0x00040168, 0x00040204 and 0x00040184, in loader A's and image 4's regions, followed by small exception wrappers. It is byte-identical in both sessions, so the boot record with its seven rewritten vector targets is stable across runs.
scope: Installed official 1.50 on XM1-body-01, two reviewed probe-bootrom sessions on 2026-10-08 reading the lead range again plus 0x80004000-0x80007fff, 0x80008000 and 0x00000000; the 0x80010000 and 0x80100000 windows are from E-STRAP-READ-150. limitations: Whether the repeat is address-bit aliasing of one 16 KiB block or a physically repeated 16 KiB image is not separated: every probed base (the lead, 0x80004000, 0x80008000, 0x80010000 and 0x80100000) is 0x4000-aligned, and bases above 1 MiB or not 0x4000-aligned are unobserved. reports/bootrom-window.md section 6 lists the discriminators.

The 0x00000000 window is live state after the application booted; its vector targets name current handlers and may differ under other firmware, and its stability is shown across two runs of the same firmware only.

All four captures (this one, 20261008T024241Z, 20261008T020826Z and 20261007T203100Z) begin at slot 0 with the same first records (type 0x09, arg0 3, arg2 65511, tick 15) and differ in clock fields (the first record's +0xc is 0x74b0 in jig A, 0x74b3 in 20261008T024241Z and 0x74b2 in the other two), the 20261008T020826Z and 20261008T024241Z pair also in the type-0x09 arg1 halfword (E-LOG-FIRST-WINDOW-DIFF-150), and the jig-A store shares no non-zero slot with the 20261008T024241Z store: 586 of 8188 slots are byte-identical and all 586 are zeros, and 36 of 512 windows match, exactly the all-zero tail past both indexes. claim: Host static closure of the X-M1 1.50 body-update selection and write path: dispatch, staging-to-media mapping, persistence order and marker discipline. The source binds descriptor slots 12/13 to indexed event/state matrices, commit record 26, modal 0x2d/0x2e input predicates, the boot-zeroed write selector 0x95d684, computed-offset UI-selector initialization, state-pointer publication and auxiliary enables. Instructions 0xecd178/0xdbd028 are direct BLs to 0xdba4a4/0x6fba08; the latter is raw read-only with optional spare-window reads. The update engine 0x00ec88c8 stages the container main range at 0x42fb7600 (file mode) or 0x42e4025c (in-memory), 0x00db90ac complements every main byte in place, and 0x006ab4cc sources block i at the image base with bit 0 cleared plus i*0x20000, so media offset equals image offset: the 32-byte trailer lands at media 0x24a0000 and its halfword at +0x1e is 0xaaaa, the halfword the first boot record compares at 0x1cec-0x1cfc (the DAT stores it complemented, 0x5555 at DAT 0x24a027a). The writer erases raw block 0x125, the trailer block, first (0x006a9aa4 calls 0x006a9010(0x125,1) and its result is unchecked), optionally pre-erases the contiguous physical run from remap[0] min(10, property 0x276) times, then programs blocks 0..0x125 in ascending logical order through the u16 remap table 0x00828580 (cumulative-skip map rebuilt by 0x006a90ac from the bad-block list pointer 0x009552f0 (list at *(0x009552f0)), first filled from the boot record scan of [0, 0x13a)), each block window-check, compare, erase, 64 pages of 0x800 program and verify with mark-bad and same-data retry at budget 0x14-[0x828578]; the source distinguishes the 16-byte spare window, bad-marker spare byte 5 and an unbounded zero retry budget, and timeout-abandon clears the interface without re-polling. The completion marker is therefore absent during the write and appears only when the trailer block programs last, its page 0 first. The configuration commit 0x00db91e0 -> 0x0069fea8 -> 0x006a8de0(0x29,33) then rewrites the configuration area, logical [0x520000, 0x940000): managed commits advance ascending logical indices with allocator-selected physical targets in pool [0x380,0x400), not physical [0x29,0x49), and program and verify the new copy before the old-copy erase and the RAM-map publication. The DAT auxiliary inputs are preserve lists (98 16-bit and 3 32-bit little-endian offset/length pairs) restoring old ranges over the refreshed 0x42000 template while cache offsets [0x42000, 0x420000) are written back as the RAM cache holds them (the boot load covers only [0, 0x76800) and [0x400000, 0x40fcc0)), and the 0xaa55 cache marker at +0x202 decides whether the next boot accepts the area or falls back to the factory template in raw blocks [7, 10). An interruption before the trailer block page 0 leaves no marker and the first boot record halts at 0x1de8 via the 0x1cc0 compare; an interruption in the configuration commit before device index 0x29 lands loses user settings to the template fallback.

The media technology name is not carried by the bytes; the flash-like reading rests on the 528-byte unit stride, the all-0xff first-16-bytes blank test, the in-page page-number decode and the bad-block remap, all static-inference, and a managed/block-device reading with per-sector tags is not excluded by the register bytes alone.

The +0x404 accept condition's field name and owner are not established; the reading that it is a per-unit tag or status whose 0xff value accepts a unit is static-inference, and the alternative that the checked bits are read data is not excluded.

The 2/4/8 KiB unit sizes and the 128 KiB to 2 MiB page groups are inferences composing the page stride, the page-format selects and the count shifts; the mode-3 (arg 0) addressing is only sketched and is unused on this body.

The staging cross-check assumes the loader advances a contiguous destination across page-select successes and the payload mapping media = payload minus 0x48; the live 0x00000000 window, the trailer at media 0x24a0000 and the second record's vector literal support both, but no live read verifies media content at 0x40000.

A page whose select fails is skipped without failing the load (0x80000ea4 -> 0x80001054), the destination advances only across real unit transfers and the count tracks staged groups, so an unselectable page inside the staged range shifts every later page down one group (128 KiB for arg 1) and the load still returns 0; nothing in the ROM checksums the staged copy and the trailer and segment gates read the media, so neither catches a compacted stage, and a successful load certifies transfer status only and never range integrity. For any future write the six-sub-unit accept tags and the bad-block marks are load-bearing: readers skip unselectable pages, so a write that damages them relocates the image in RAM instead of failing visibly.

The port-mirror attribution rests on order of execution and on the value's bit pattern; an image-5 execution before some capture is not excluded by the dumps, and the bytes do not resolve which core reads 0x4003 from p14, so the record-1 against record-2 twin is unresolved (both write identical bytes).
The R1 judgement is an evidence-level assessment, not a gate acceptance, and it demonstrates no execution, no storage repair and no write route independent of the application.

The action opens the storage driver at 0xdbcfe0 and closes it at 0xdbd030 itself, and 0x4b2ece00 is the head of an eight-entry 0x1827c00-byte frame-buffer pool rather than private scratch. Seven whitelist values reach storage-write-capable or state-destroying handlers: 0x06, 0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x24, 0x28 and 0xc3; six of the seven take the inert action 3 only in state 4 and 0xc3 also in state 6, and state 4 is also the state that defeats the read, so the state word at 0x015c20b0 is a precondition and not a safety gate, and cache byte 0x81 is overloaded four ways and must stay 0. The reader takes physical block numbers. The descriptor-layer area read resolves its map-relative index with FUN_006fca60, which reads the u16 at map + 0x10 + 2 * index, returns minus one for a 0xffff entry and otherwise adds the map object start word (file offsets 0xe0668 to 0xe0690: ldr r2,[r1]; ldr r3,[r1,#8]; add r0,r1,r0,lsl #1; ldrh r0,[r0,#16]; movw r3,#0xffff; cmp r0,r3; addne r0,r0,r2; mvneq r0,#0), and feeds the resolved block to FUN_006f1a74 as block * PPB + page (mla at 0xe0798, bl at 0xe07a8), while FUN_006fed00 feeds the same entry point block * PPB with no map resolution (mov r0,r5 at 0xe2978, bl at 0xe2988). The blocks holding the area-2 banks are therefore the map-resolved entry + 0x380, not the encoded descriptor bases 0x3d6 and 0x3d7, which equal those only under the identity map. The hazard set is seven values with the blast radius of each: 0x06 writes one byte into the retained settings image and reaches the device-write primitive FUN_006f0f6c; 0x20 reaches FUN_006f0f6c through its closure; 0x21 runs FUN_0069fe20 and discards unsaved adjustment state by reloading from storage; 0x22 runs FUN_0069fea8 and commits the whole 4 MiB adjustment area from the RAM mirror; 0x24 is FUN_00dbc924, a RAM read/write that can overwrite any accepted address including the staging window; 0x28 is the erase dispatcher FUN_00dbcaa4 whose cases 2 and 3 erase both area-2 banks; 0xc3 reaches FUN_006f0f6c through its closure. The state word at 0x015c20b0 is a precondition, not a gate: state 4 disables the read as well as every destructive row, and state 6 disarms 0xc3 alone while the read still runs, so no state both reads and disarms the hazard set.

The action leaves the storage driver shut down: the close at 0xdbd030 clears the ready flag with no refcount and no already-open guard, so nothing else may hold storage during the session and the body needs a power cycle before normal use.

The staging window 0x4b2ece00 is shared with imaging, sitting at the head of the frame-buffer pool, so a capture, live view or playback in flight writes the same bytes; which pool layout is live and whether 0x100000 bytes are backed and idle are runtime facts.

Facts a run must read from the camera first: the state halfword at 0x015c20b0, the session-start values of cache 0x80..0x8a, the area-2 map entries, staging-window backing and idle status, any other queue-7 poster during the session, and any other holder of the storage driver.

claim: X-M1 1.50 has no color-space property or setting (static-inference over byte-read bytes of the pinned images; the owner's menu search is reported). On 2026-10-08 the owner searched XM1-body-01 running official 1.50 under ordinary controls and found no COLOR SPACE row in the menus he walks for RECIPE-00 or in SET-UP. In the firmware, no property id, no values array, no menu node, no label entry and no stored field is bound to color space. What exists is label text and a metadata field. Label text: COLOR SPACE, sRGB and Adobe RGB are UTF-16 strings in the English language slot and the German and Japanese dumps carry the translated trio (string ids 0x647/0x648/0x649), and the plain image carries ASCII copies at 0x011206cc-0x011206e8. Nothing uses them: the id4 node map names no node with any of the three labels, an aligned halfword and word scan of the whole 2,631,680-byte id4 image for 0x647/0x648/0x649 finds no label entry, no values array and no node header (only code, tone-curve data and a run of adjustment-cache index pairs at 0x007ce224 in the shape the FUN_006cc604-family readers index), the 289 conversion tables reachable through the pointer array at 0x0081b09c carry no color-space rows, and the 57-field C-payload map carries no color-space field. Metadata: the plain image's image-parameter info screen decodes the record word at +0x184 as 0 sRGB, 1 AdobeRGB, other blank (FUN_01118a00; ldr r3,[r3,#0x184] at 0x011930c), the EXIF summary's color-space halfword at +0x4ca is initialised to the constant 1 (sRGB) by FUN_011c2ecc and overwritten only by a parsed file's tag 0xa001 (FUN_011c36f8), FUN_012770a0 tests it equal to 1 for a print flag, and the id5 makernote builders write no color-space field. The camera's own frames record EXIF ColorSpace sRGB (tag 0xa001 = 1) with InteroperabilityIndex R98 and no color-space tag in the FujiFilm makernote (hardware-observed frames read host-side). The recorded value is therefore fixed sRGB, not derived from any setting: the metadata field's capture-time producer is unproved, and one 1.50-era frame would close that link end to end.
scope: The pinned official 1.50 images (id4 at 0x0061c400, id5 at 0x00bf1a00, plain at 0x01100000, the English language slot), the id4 node map and C-payload map of this tree, the S01/S02 frames shot on XM1-body-01 under firmware 1.00, and the owner's 2026-10-08 menu search on the same body running installed official 1.50 under ordinary controls; claims are 1.50 except where the frame evidence names 1.00

claim: A host encoder for the X-M1 1.50 compressed-record format reproduces both stock compressed records byte for byte from their decoded images, and the decompressor's own code accepts no stored image (the code facts are static-inference from the pinned bytes; the reproduction is a host run). Three guards close defect classes without touching the matcher or the stock fill shapes: a literal run at the 127 cap with 129 bytes of page left flushes one byte short (a full-cap flush there strands one byte of page and the old code answered with a zero-length run), a zero-length run flush is a hard error, and the encoder refuses a total_len on a feed boundary (FeedAlignedTotalLen) or a record over its flash window (WindowExceeded) and re-walks its tokens (InvalidTokenization); the pinned reproduction still passes on both images with the guards applied.
scope: Pinned public X-M1 1.50 payload (payload-complement.bin) and the two decoded images, host-only runs 2026-10-09; stock token statistics are 317,995 and 623,410 matches with 0 of them longer than their distance and minimum distance 3; the stock records use 92 and 96 percent of their flash windows.
limitations: The engine's interpretation of mode values other than 4 is hardware: the driver reduces the byte to bit 24 of the length register and nothing more is observable from the code.

The grammar's unused corners (control 0x00, distance 0, length 0, overlapping copies, distances 1-2) are refused by fflzd, never occur in the stock streams and are never emitted here; engine behaviour on them is unproved.

Token behaviour across a feed kick and interior pages that do not fill to their end is untested: the stock streams never exhibit either and the encoder never produces them. The engine's end-of-stream behaviour when the final kick is a full chunk is untested and the encoder refuses that geometry, so the refusal is a guard against an untested shape rather than a test of it.

For a modified input the byte-for-byte reproduction is evidence of model fidelity only: the engine has been observed on two streams, and the patched record is safe to build and review, not safe to trust. No camera has accepted a rebuilt container; the install decision remains open.

claim: The SET-UP menu's CUSTOM RESET item is bound to its handler, and what it does to the stored C record is stated in the pinned X-M1 1.50 images (static-inference over byte-read sites and the private decompilation of the same bytes; host-only). The item is item 13 of the setup root node 0x00789228 (kind 7, property 5): its values entry at 0x007886e0 is {0x91, 0} and its label record at 0x00786688 is {0x1a4, 0, 0, 0} with string id 0x1a4 = "<f136>CUSTOM RESET" in the English slot; the owner reports the item on the body's SET-UP 2 page. The action is FUN_00c32320 (0x00c32320, image 5): it reads the framework's action parameter cells 0x0094f650 and 0x0094f654 (the block 0x0094f64c-0x0094f65c is written by FUN_0063270c, id4) and calls the reset dispatcher FUN_00d4e4d4, whose first branch handles the value 0x91, the item's id in the values array; the handler word 0x00c32320 sits at pointer 0xd04764 in the image-5 pointer run that also holds the CUSTOM SET action 0x00c74e5c at 0xd04214 (that function's tail calls FUN_00d4e2a0(4,0,0), the copy of the current settings into slot 0). The custom branch clears 0x00954294, stores reset class 3 into 0x00944564 through FUN_00638220, and calls FUN_00d4e2a0(row, row, 1) with both rows from 0x0094f654; that routine returns before any write unless the destination row is 0, writes property 0xe9 for slot 0 from the getter's defaults branch (0x007cb80e >> 5 = 3) and calls FUN_00630b14(row, 0, 1). FUN_00630b14 walks about ninety properties, takes each value from FUN_0061e110(prop, 0, 1, srcSlot), the defaults read through the pointer 0x007cb804 at 0x28*slot + payload offset, writes it into destination slot code 0, and, because that code is not 1, stores the 0x28-byte record from 0x0096cda4 to settings-image offset 0x140 through FUN_0072b3d0 -> FUN_006a6f3c -> FUN_006a86c4, which compares record bytes [2, 0x2c) and appends the record to area 3 through FUN_006ac7d4 on a difference; the dispatcher tail then runs the settings notify 0x00d466c8. Scope: slot row 0, per-slot, with no all-slots loop; the ordinary settings block and slot rows 1 and 2 are untouched; the mirror and area 3 are written on the spot, so the record reads as the per-slot defaults (film simulation PROVIA, image quality FINE, index byte +0x27 zero, mode field 3). Relation to the three bound routes: CUSTOM RESET is the CUSTOM SET copy FUN_00630b14 with the defaults source (flag 1) in place of the current-or-slot source (flag 0), sharing the same store and area-3 commit, so it is a third stock writer of the mirror at 0x140 beside the CUSTOM SET copy and the boot record read 0x006a8abc; it is neither the defaults constructor 0x006a6fd8 (ordinary block plus adjustment-cache fields, boot-time after an area-2 failure) nor the mirror reload FUN_00630a34 through FUN_0061d994, which runs image into RAM. The UI session reset FUN_00d3c20c is not this item's path: its caller is FUN_00d3c3b4 at case 0xc of switch(*(0x009500f0)), the previous-UI-mode cell, so it is the teardown of UI mode 0xc, a shutdown-class mode the requester FUN_00d350c4 writes for the power, ring, barrier, adapter and cradle inputs, and the CUSTOM RESET chain writes no mode cell; the reset's reachability in ordinary shooting is a property of that mode machine, not of this item. Consequence for RC1: selecting CUSTOM RESET clears a stored C recipe, index byte and payload fields included, and commits the default record to area 3, which the design handles as index 0 = no recipe, as a user-invokable route beside the jig-cycle constructor.
scope: Host-only static analysis of the pinned official 1.50 images (id4 at 0x0061c400, id5 at 0x00bf1a00), the private decompilation of the same bytes and the owner's menu report; no camera access, no emulation, no camera operation proposed.

limitations: The framework call site that fills 0x0094f650 with 0x91 for this item is not traced, so the item-to-handler link rests on the id in the handler's keyed branch and on the handler's word position in the image-5 menu-action pointer run; the per-modal dispatcher FUN_00bfb028 selects handler arrays by modal id and no table of it was bound to this item.

The stock media config block is two 512-byte halves (payload.bin 0x48-0x247 and 0x848-0xa47), each four identical copies in its 2 KiB media unit (byte-read), and the apply this body survives at every mode-4 boot (hardware-observed) performs seven pair writes ((0xfffb2004,0x5f5f), (0xfffb2008,1), (0xfffb200c,0x11), (0xfffb2010,0x1111), (0xfffb2014,0x1111), (0xfff98100,0x50000100), (0xfff98104,0)) and writes 0x22312131 and 0x00000605 to 0xfff52050 and 0xfff52078, the values the running driver init uses. ffsys.bin for the SD routes is these same 1024 bytes concatenated (mode 1 reads 0x400 bytes to 0xfff00004, mode 2 reads card blocks 0 and 1 there), so a survivable config image exists in-project and its apply is byte-identical to the every-boot case; the stock-plus-zero-tail variant is withdrawn, since it drops the pair writes and zeros the half-2 words.
scope: Pinned boot-ROM block and pinned public 1.50 payload; static decode and byte inspection 2026-10-09; the hardware-observed element is only that this body boots through the same apply on internal media at every power-up.

limitations: The pair targets 0xfffb2004-0xfffb2014, 0xfff98100-0xfff98104 and the 0xfff99000 and 0xfff52000 config words are writes into unidentified peripheral blocks; none lies in a media or adjustment range, and the register-class reading is static-inference.

Modes 1 and 2 apply the config with no internal-media controller initialized, where mode 4 initializes it first; the stock values written to the 0xfff52000 words are the same in both contexts and the context difference is untested.
No ffsys.bin has been carried on a card or applied through mode 1 or mode 2; the survival evidence is the internal-media route only.
The unbounded status waits mean a wrong config image can hang the apply; a power cycle is the undo, and no decoded ROM path writes persistent state.

label: independently-reproduced
claim: A verification gate that re-derives the value it must check cannot fail, and one did in the image-replacement chain (host run and byte reads over the pinned 1.50 container; corrected build independently reproduced). The container's record-4 header word 1 is the record length the loader's feed arithmetic reads (total_len = 0x14 + stream length; stock 0x146567 with stream 0x146553), not the stream length the field contract's label said; a short value feeds the decompressor fewer bytes than the stream holds, drops tokens and lands in the engine's hang-shaped failure inside the unrecoverable window. The first chain run wrote the stream length into that word (0x1465cc where 0x1465e0 belonged) and the rebuilt-stream gate passed anyway because it re-assembled the record header from its own derivation instead of reading the container's stored words, so the wrong stored word never reached the decoder. The fix reads the artifact and compares: word 1 is checked against 0x14 + the stream bytes, the emission checks run against the bytes read back from the assembly instead of the derived header, and the fflzd gate consumes the five stored words with the decoder's own arithmetic checking them. The same-shape sweep over the chain: record-header word 0 compares against the attached decoded image, word 2 against the stored word 1's ceil, words 3 and 4 against constants, and the three checksum words against a fresh complement-sum over the assembled bytes; the segment entry's size and bss words and the trailer words that mirror entry 4 are relations between stored words (size = decoded + 0x28, bss = load + decoded, bss end = id-5 load, trailer = entry-4 load/size) with no re-derivation in the check path; the carried set compares against the source container and the pinned stock restore lists. No other derivation-that-masks instance was found in the chain. The lesson for any new gate: verify by reading the artifact and comparing, never by recomputing from the same derivation that produced it, because a recomputation agrees with itself whatever the artifact says.
scope: Host tooling over the pinned public X-M1 1.50 container and one probe rebuild; the claim is about the gate design, not about camera behavior; host-only.
limitations: The defect class is established by construction and by the corrected run; that no other instance exists is a sweep result over this chain's checks, not a property any future gate inherits automatically.

The loader's feed arithmetic (word 1 minus 0x14 bytes fed, no others) is static-inference from the mapped driver copies; the hang-shaped failure is the engine error branch's documented shape, not a hardware-observed hang.
The parse layer the comparisons trust is itself proven only by the byte-exact round trip on stock and the synthetic suite.
A short word 1 in a container that passed review and installed would hang the boot in the invalid-application class with the recorded recovery limits; nothing was installed and no camera was touched.

claim: A diagnostic X-M1 1.50 SD-BOOT card is built from held material without the ZJ02217 service files, and //host/firmware:build-boot-card verifies its bytes against a host model of the ROM's parser (static-inference over byte-read ROM; reports/diagnostic-sd-boot-card.md, reports/bootrom-window.md sections 3.1-3.3). ROM requirements, byte-read: mode 1 opens only ffsys.bin and ffboot.bin, mode 2 reads raw blocks and mode 4 reads internal media, so ffuser.bin is not a ROM requirement on these routes. Mode 1 reads 1024 ffsys.bin bytes into 0xfff00004 for the apply 0x80000304, then stages ffboot.bin's directory size at 0x40000000 in chunks up to 0x8000 and hands off in A32 to 0x00000000 without checking a record header, checksum, model, version, trailer, segment table or destination-size bound. FAT mount 0x80001ba0 (called at 0x8000083c) applies the volume check 0x80001ae0 (55 aa at +510 and FA at +54 or +82) to sector 0 and accepts a FAT superfloppy; failing that, it reads the first MBR entry at +0x1be itself, requires a nonzero type, takes its +8 start LBA and applies the same check to that boot sector. The stack assumes 512-byte sectors, selects FAT12/16/32 from the BPB read in 0x80001ba0 by data-cluster count plus 2 at thresholds 0xff7/0xfff7, uses the first FAT, follows cluster chains (0x80001678, so fragmentation is supported) and compares root-directory 11-byte names FFSYS   BIN and FFBOOT  BIN in the 8.3 open 0x80001dc4; no active flag is required and GPT, exFAT and later partitions are not parsed. Mode 2 (0x8000071c) reads card blocks 0 and 1 as config and applies them through 0x80000304 with no marker check: config offset x goes to 0xfff01000+(x-0xe0) (0x800005dc-0x800005e4), the window is words +0x00..+0x244 with the last byte +0x247 (0x800005ec cmp #0x92), and the consumed count is at SRAM 0xfff0001c, so a plain FAT card in mode 2 would apply its MBR sector and a zero sector as register configuration. ffsys.bin is the 1024-byte stock config payload.bin[0x48,0x248)+[0x848,0xa48), preserving its seven pair writes and the 0xfff52050=0x22312131 and 0xfff52078=0x605 driver cross-checks (E-CONFIG-APPLY-150); its config-driven values and branches match the mode-4 apply the body survives at every boot (hardware-observed). With these bytes +0x33c = 0x80000000, so the optional helper runs and rewrites the channel-0 divider; before ffboot.bin is read the apply also sets 0xfff88028 to 0x60000, final 0xfff88030 to 0xa00 and channel-0 divider bits 15:6 to zero. A bounded dataflow replay of the unchanged ROM windows 0x80000328-0x80000334, 0x800003cc-0x800003f8 and 0x800006a8-0x800006cc against the actual ffsys.bin (emulated) confirmed these stores, including SD halfwords 503, 3, 3, 7 from fixture initial 507; 0xa00 retains bit 0x200 and application code selects clock field 6 for several presets, so these writes alone do not show a disabled SD clock or an invalid frequency. Current builder output, dual-path: a 17,826,304-byte FAT16 MBR image (one partition at LBA 2048, 32768 sectors, one sector per cluster, both files in the root) plus one reserved report sector at LBA 34816 outside the partition, left zero. Mode 1 reads the unchanged stock ffsys.bin and the 512-byte halt ffboot.bin through FAT; raw LBAs 0-1 hold the stock config with exactly five changed bytes (the mode-2 count at +0x18 set to one and the mandatory MBR type, start and signature fields overlaid; the partition entry spans config bytes +0xde..+0xed across words +0xdc to +0xec and the signature sits in word +0x11c), and raw LBA 2 holds the same payload. Config apply on mode 2 propagates three changed words: 0xfff010e0=0x00040000 instead of zero, 0xfff010e4=0x08000000 instead of zero and 0xfff0111c=0xaa550101 instead of 0x01000101 (E-SDBOOT-CONFIG-WINDOW-150, E-SDBOOT-CONTROLLER-FAMILY-150). The verifier re-parses the emitted bytes through a reimplementation of the ROM's volume check, mount and BPB parse, root open, chain follow and read 0x80001e88, and rejects the earlier FAT-only image; independent format review confirmed the five byte differences and both modelled layouts and found a FAT16 cluster-high mismatch, fixed by an unconditional high-word read. The halt payload (host/firmware/diagnostic-halt.S) is 15 A32 instructions whose whole write set is one stmia of sixteen bytes at RAM 0x00000100 carrying 58 4d 31 44 (XM1D), 42 4f 4f 54 (BOOT) and the words 0x150 and 1, then dsb, the ROM's own wfi and its self-loop; no MMIO access, load, call, CP15 access or supervisor call, and its SP lies past the one-sector staged span. Its RAM signature is not recoverable: RAM 0x00000100 lies inside the staged span at 0x40000000, the alias of RAM 0, and every ROM route that reaches the application stages its first block there before the handoff. Mode 4 sets destination 0x40000000 with count [config+0x18] & 0x3ffff = 2 page groups of 128 KiB (the config word at payload.bin + 0x60 reads 0x00000002), writing RAM [0x00000000, 0x00040000) from media [0x40000, 0x80000), and the byte staged to RAM 0x00000100 is the first boot record's, sixteen 0xff bytes (decode/boot-40048.bin offset 0x100); mode 1's DMA dispatcher reads whole sectors for destinations in [0x40000000, 0x80000000) whatever the requested sub-sector count, and mode 2 reads raw blocks by DMA to 0x40000000. The only RAM reader, opcode 0x200001 function 2 (address at +0x1c), acts inside a maintenance session under the running application and read staged record content in the 256 bytes at 0x00000000 in an ordinary boot (E-BOOTROM-DISCRIMINATOR-150, window 00000000.bin); the halted payload exits only by a battery pull. The ROM's SD code is initialization plus reads (command table 0x800022e0-0x8000232f, read command 0x113a at base+0x0e) and its internal-media code (init 0x80000b74, page select 0x80000c2c, block read 0x80000d08, paged loader 0x80000dec) only reads, with failure paths that write only MMIO, so an observable outcome needs a channel the payload supplies: a visible indicator (E-SDBOOT-BLINK-STARTUP-CANDIDATE-150) or a validated record (magic, nonce, revision, entry-state words, checksum, completion marker) written to the reserved sector at LBA 34816 and read back on a host card reader. A valid record would prove entry plus execution and darkness without one is not evidence. A control card without ffboot.bin cannot identify mode 1: selector 7 reaches the same halt (0x80000290/0x80000294 into 0x800001fc) and selector 4 with a nonzero high pair runs mode 2 at 0x80000170 without reading the file. The card carries no writer and is not a repair medium.
scope: Host-only: the pinned official 1.50 DAT and complemented payload, the captured 0x4000 boot-ROM artifact, the pinned first boot record and the existing low-RAM capture; the image, config and payload are private-data artifacts. This record executes no payload; hardware runs of cards from this builder are E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150, E-SDBOOT-STAGE-MARKER-150 and E-SDBOOT-BLINK-WARM-OBSERVED-150. The factory MAIN PWB Initialize package remains unobtained and is distinct from this card.
commands: Read pinned bootrom.dis mode-1 loader 0x8000082c-0x80000934, FAT mount/name/chain/read closure 0x80001678-0x80002090, and SD wait helper 0x80001618-0x80001648; compared with E-CONFIG-APPLY-150 and E-SDBOOT-FILE-COVERAGE-150
Temporary C/Unicorn probe executed ROM windows 80000328..80000334, 800003cc..800003f8 and 800006a8..800006cc against actual ffSYS; output retained, driver/executable removed
limitations: Verification is host-side: a format check against a model of the ROM's parser, not card-reader, SD-controller, camera or execution evidence.

Modes 1 and 2 enter without the mode-4 internal-media initialization; incoming MMIO state and unbounded config polls remain hardware questions, and the SD wait helper 0x80001618 polls status without a software iteration limit.

The ROM file-read helper can return success after EOF-shortening without the mode-1 caller checking the transferred length; the host must enforce the complete 1024-byte config, a nonempty bounded executable and a sector-rounded DMA destination span.
The three MBR-derived MMIO word effects of the raw overlay remain unidentified; stock-like other words do not establish harmlessness or bounded readiness waits.
The retained stock MBR geometry is not a conventional partition table. Formatting or copying files loses the raw-mode overlay, so preparation needs a whole-image write and readback.
The payload's RAM write audit does not bound prior ROM configuration effects or prove that reset restores all persistent state.

Whether a later stage or the running application also writes RAM 0x00000100 is unproved; the first staging already overwrites it. Retention of any RAM address across a battery pull is unproved, so no RAM address is established as observable, and extending the read primitive to a 0x00000100 window would need a code change.

The clock replay ran in a Cortex-A9 dataflow interpreter with flat fixture memory and a seeded SD-ready bit after Cortex-R5F attempts raised UC_ERR_EXCEPTION at the first window; it does not establish R4F fidelity, and physical frequency and cold-start SD effects remain unbound.
The service payload's ffuser.bin role and behaviour on a nonblank board remain unproved; omitting it is justified only for the decoded ROM routes and the project diagnostic.
A dark body does not separate payload execution from a config-apply hang or a failed read, and the card's contents are identical after every outcome because the ROM writes no media.

The halt card carries no SD writer, and the ROM supplies none. Report-sector reporters built separately use the X-M1 stock CMD25 PIO request (E-SDBOOT-XM1-PIO-WRITE-BINDING-150); their replacement of the stock writer's RTOS flags and interrupts with bounded polling, and command and busy completion, are unproved on hardware.
The card supplies no writer; no R3 or R4 claim follows from it.

label: static-inference
claim: The AUTO_ACT gate byte 0xa2 can be set and cleared as a RAM-only write whose reversal is symmetric, and the persistent form is blocked on boundedness rather than on reversibility (static-inference over byte-read of the pinned decoded images, capture bytes byte-read from this body's three adjustment captures; reports/auto-act-arming.md). Byte-read: the config callback 0x00dc7564 stores through 0x0069fc94 before any other test and posts the queue-7 commit message 0x1707 only for a start index of 0x80, so a config 0x1a0002 function 3 write at index 0xa2 lands at RAM 0x41acd8a2 with no storage write and no whitelist scan, and the boot load 0x0069f204 refills the mirror from storage, so a power cycle reverts the byte. The 0xa2 readers by constant index number two: 0x00ed2b84, the mujin gate function, and 0x00ed45b0, a ten-byte snapshot of FUN_00ed4570 whose consumer is unproved. Index 0x265, which gates the second sender route FUN_00d0cd10 from the event pump 0x00c22f60, reads 0x00 in all three captures, so that route is dead as shipped and arming 0xa2 does not open it. The mujin task is created once per boot and tests a2 == 2 once before its receive loop, so an armed camera attempts the card read once per power-on in both ordinary and maintenance boots. After a passing test, both senders 0x00ed2b8c and 0x00ed2be4 re-read the gate byte when they run and FUN_00ed2c34 re-tests it before them, so a disarm between the test and the sends suppresses the run silently. On an armed boot with no card or no DCAA file the open fails, no read and no parse occur and the script area is left cleared; a file of at most 1 MiB is read to 0x43e6ff00 with its size stored at 0x16777ac only when the completion count equals the request; a file above 1 MiB is closed unread and parsed as zero length; a file with more statements than the store's usable prefix writes into the script's own variable array at 0x16776dc and label table at 0x1677744, so the practical bound is under about 300 lines; and a record whose code matches no dispatch entry stops the table walk and leaves the loop blocked in receive, a quiet stall rather than camera-state corruption. Reaching storage with index 0xa2 requires the whole-area commit 0x0069fea8 of 0x420000 bytes from the RAM mirror, triggered by a config write of 0x22 to index 0x80, which the End Setting live protocol forbids in any value; the reversal is the same function with the byte patched to 0x00 in the mirror, so set and unset carry the same mechanism and the failing property is that neither is bounded to the byte. label: static-inference
claim: The AUTO_ACT RAM-only arming session is the closed H2 operation arm-auto-act, with its refusals, host tests, offline rehearsal and session document (static-inference over the byte-read design of reports/auto-act-arming.md section 13 and the pinned official 1.50 decoded images; the tests and the rehearsal run against a scripted camera). Request sequence: an optional wait before power-on of at most 120 s, continuing only on no eligible device; C0 open requiring the constant tail; the page-0 window read requiring adjustment index 0xa2 = 0x00 and 0xf7 = 0x00; the config write 0xf7 = 0x01 with its readback; a first gated RAM read sampling the boot tick 0x400c0800; the two witness windows 0x1667000 and 0x1677700 read as 128-byte 0x200001 function 2 halves and required all-zero; the config write 0xa2 = 0x02 with the page-0 readback requiring 0x02; the watch, one poll per second capped at 90 polls, reading 0x1667000 for the guard 0x1667048 and 0x1677780 for the loader's async block, until the guard is 1 with in-flight 0x16777b0 at 0 and the loader acted (status 0x16777b4 nonzero, or input length 0x16777ac nonzero with statement index 0x1667054 at -1, or selector 0x16777c0 at 2 with a zero length word); the full after windows; an end tick sample after the final witnesses; the config write 0xf7 = 0x00 with its readback; C4. Both tick samples are reported as ticks and as seconds at 99.88 Hz. Standalone precondition, gate and before-witness capture writes happen after the arm, while raw reply durability and refusal checks stay before it. The only config start indices are 0xa2 and 0xf7 (a bounded enum), mkWriteTarget refuses 0x80 by name and every other index, every config write frame is the 37-byte length-1 form, and no write of 0x00 to index 0xa2 is sent: the disarm is the session-ending power cycle that refills the mirror from storage. Verdict: six outcomes, ran-to-end, file-op-failed, load-running, load-failed, no-send and no-load, read in the order guard, then index and count, then status, then selector. Byte-read basis: the file-completion callbacks 0x00ed17b0 (the file job and WT_LOG) and 0x00ed17d8 (the loader's read) both store their transferred byte count at 0x16777bc and their status at 0x16777b4, so any later file operation overwrites both; the WT_LOG handler 0xed28b4 passes 0xfff to its writer 0xed1850 at 0xed28d0 before it increments the statement index, and END 0xed1610 writes the index -1, so a settled ran-to-end carries the log write's count while the 13-byte load's size stays in the input length word 0x16777ac, written when the read's completion count equals the requested size. A failed load cannot show the index at -1: the loader's clear of 0x10764 bytes at 0x166704c leaves it 0 and only END writes -1, so the index -1 with a count greater than 0 names a script that ran, a zero status at that index names ran-to-end, and a nonzero status there, a failed operation of the script's own, names the new outcome file-op-failed. Witness cells (static-inference): selector 1 with records present and wait cell 0x1667050 = 0xffffffff is a completed END, selector 2 with records present is running or stalled, selector 1 with a zeroed area is an armed boot whose file open failed, and selector 0 with a zeroed area is never armed. reports/auto-act-session-script.md carries the witness-cell interpretation table, the card preparation with the 13-byte script's SHA-256 bdd37b75ad3e2664ea8fc42fc9611d4fd761abde4fe487b0d357348beddd11e8 and the numbered act list. The operation has run twice on the body, both times without a sender (E-AUTOACT-160839-150).

claim: The mujin task's delay argument unit is the kernel scheduler's unit, about 1.0 to 1.3 ms, so the AUTO_ACT one-shot gate test falls about 1 s after task start and the 4000-unit wait about 4 s (static-inference over byte-read of the pinned 1.50 loader and application images, with tick rates and host latency hardware-observed from this body's capture journals). Delay calls, byte-read: the task entry FUN_00ed2ce0 calls FUN_00ed2c90 (bl at 0xed2cec), whose first action is mov r0,#1000 / bl 0x00ed1660 at 0xed2ca8-0xed2cac; FUN_00ed1660 is a one-instruction wrapper (push {r11,lr}; add r11,sp,#4; bl 0x00723ce8; pop {r11,pc} at 0xed1660-0xed166c); the second wait is mov r0,#4000 / bl 0x00ed1660 at 0xed2cbc-0xed2cc0 and the sender's trailing wait is mov r0,#100 at 0xed2c84; the kernel delay 0x00723ce8 loads the interface pointer at 0x0096bd20, calls its +0x1618 selector, and for a nonzero argument calls interface[selector]+0x4c with the delay argument in r0, while a zero argument takes the +0x11c arm instead. Unit chain, byte-read: the app wrapper 0x00723ce8 calls service [descriptor + 0x4c] with the argument unchanged; loader A installs 0x00046e48 there at 0x00040524-0x0004052c, storing the word 0x00046e48 into the field at +0x4c of the record at 0x4004dae0; that function saves the argument in r8 at 0x46e50, marks the current task delayed with a 2 at record +0xc at 0x46f44-0x46f48, loads the clock pointer from the current record at +0x40 and inserts the wake deadline as the argument plus that clock through 0x44c60 at 0x46f84-0x46f94, with no scaling by ten. The clock pair 0x4005476c and 0x40054770 is initialized 0 and 10 at 0x44a50, and the timer service 0x44d8c copies next time to current time and adds 10 per call at 0x44eec-0x44ef0. The interrupt callback 0x40b24 calls that service once at 0x40b34-0x40b38 and then increments the log tick 0x400c0800 once at 0x40b50, so the tick rate and the clock step are one interrupt. Loader B carries the same relationship at 0xd0524-0xd052c, 0xd6f44-0xd6f54 and 0xd4eb0, and the two images' timer block at file offsets 0xbb0-0xc4c is byte-identical apart from base immediates and relative branch displacements, including the reload 30000, which is 16 times 1875. Hardware-observed tick rates: the tick cell 0x400c0800 reads 72436, 72461 and 87394 in the three checkpoints of read-log session 20261009T064945Z (journal tuples at line 65 and line 17027, 149.72 s apart on the session's monotonic clock), 14958 units in 149.72 s, 99.9 Hz; two short spans in the same session give 0.87 to 1.06 kHz, which the 16-bit field at +0x06 of the ring entries explains as the same counter's low halfword; and 20261008T024241Z-read-log advances at least 75 units per host second. With the clock stepping 10 per tick, one delay unit is 1.0 to 1.3 ms and 1000 units 1.0 to 1.3 s; the earlier reading of a 10 ms unit, with the test about 10 s after task start and the arm write two orders of magnitude inside it, is refuted. The task's id class reads 1 in the table 0x007cad9c (byte-read; the receive wrapper 0x00725318 shifts it into the high halfword of the service argument and the kernel resolves class 1 to the record 0x400545cc), and the wrappers dispatch to the calling core's kernel, the kernel whose log carries the app's own message records (E-AF-LENS-TRAFFIC-150), so the task's delay is that kernel's entry against 0x4005476c and 0x40054770. Hardware-observed host cost: over all 53 service sessions under private-data/sessions, the interval from the session's first journal line to the first outgoing transfer (the C0 ControlWrite) runs 89.35 ms minimum, 92.95 ms median, 122.56 ms 90th percentile and 182.76 ms maximum, with 47 of 53 between 89 and 104 ms. The task's creation is the bl at 0x00d98660 inside FUN_00d985a4, and the boot-log captures carry the image-5 load on maintenance boots as on ordinary ones (LOAD-TIMING-01). Consequence for the 16:08 run (E-AUTOACT-160839-150): the test instant is 1.0 to 1.3 s after task start, the arm was confirmed at about 4.81 to 5.10 s uptime, and the prologue store was already present at the baseline read at 4.265 s, so the task started no later than about 3.5 to 3.8 s, the same order as the instant the host's wait list first saw the device at about 3.66 s; the run's absent sender therefore witnesses a test that preceded the arm, and no reordering of the reviewed host sequence can be justified before the window's position is measured (reports/auto-act-arming.md section 13.4 proposes that read).
scope: Pinned official X-M1 1.50 loader decodes (RAM bases 0x00040000 and 0x000d0000), the decoded images 4 and 5 and the app service wrappers, plus this body's own capture journals (read-log 20261009T064945Z, 20261008T024241Z and all 53 sessions under private-data/sessions); host-only reading, no camera command.

The two kernel images are separate builds with different layouts, so only loader A's delay entry address is bound here; loader B's equivalent addresses and its ten-unit clock step are carried from E-LOG-TICK-SOURCE-150 and its own listing.

The class table's producer and semantics are not decoded: the claim that the task is created in the calling core's kernel rests on the wrappers' per-CPU dispatch and on the app's own records appearing in that kernel's log.

Method: each pair is compared block by block (24x14 blocks of 204x197 px, per-block NCC-optimal integer offset within 24 px of a global seed, medians of L*, C* and of the hue of the median (a*,b*) per block), keeping only blocks with local NCC >= 0.95; differences are B minus A over matched blocks, +- standard error. Fixed-scene triple, 2026-10-09 11:01 to 11:02, film tag written by the camera on each frame: DSCF3095.JPG F0/Standard (Provia), DSCF3096.JPG Pro Neg. Std, DSCF3097.JPG Pro Neg. Hi, with identical exposure (1/100, f/4.5, ISO 6400, DynamicRangeSetting Manual with DevelopmentDynamicRange 100, WB Daylight) and identical adjustments (Color, Highlight and Shadow +2 on all three in the retained RAF metadata, private-data/analysis/closure42/retained-metadata.csv, E-FILMSIM-PRODUCERS-MMIO-150); the camera moved on its support between frames. 3095 to 3096 dL* +2.18 +- 0.59 (t 3.68, n=70), dC* -1.65 +- 0.37 at C* >= 5 (n=43), dh* +4.4 +- 2.3 at C* >= 8 (n=30); 3095 to 3097 dL* -0.87 +- 0.46 (n=41), dC* -0.99 +- 0.45 (n=28), dh* +0.6 +- 0.9 (n=22); 3096 to 3097 dL* -2.19 +- 0.35 (n=100), dC* +1.27 +- 0.38 (n=65), dh* -3.7 +- 1.0 (n=38). Flat matched blocks (mean |grad L| <= 0.013), where content mismatch cannot move a median: +1.73 +- 0.32 (n=22), -1.32 +- 0.57 (n=10) and -3.23 +- 0.32 (n=26) L*; the signs are uniform across frame halves and the three pairs satisfy the triangle within their errors, so the identical-render hypothesis is rejected. Repeat run, 2026-10-09/10: nine shots in three rounds of PROVIA, PRO Neg Std and PRO Neg Hi selected through the SHOOTING MENU, with sequential frame IDs 963-3102 through 963-3110: 3102, 3105 and 3108 PROVIA, 3103, 3106 and 3109 PRO Neg Std, 3104, 3107 and 3110 PRO Neg Hi. One scene (a table with a green Nalgene, white paper and a purple hat), M mode, 1/60 s, f/4.5, ISO 1600, DR 100%, WB Daylight, Color, highlight, shadow, sharpness and noise reduction all 0, WB shift 0 centered; focus by per-shot AREA acquisition on the same paper edge with S1 held from focus confirmation to full press, adopted after the manual-focus retention failure (E-MF-RETENTION-COUNTER-150). The owner reports every shot focus confirmed, playback detail sharp, no warning, and no camera or scene movement, lighting change, settings change or sleep/wake across the run. The nine original JPEGs are transferred (frame files DSCF3102 through DSCF3110 copied 9 of 9 to private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/render-repeat-9/ from the owner's camera directory, 4896x2760 8-bit sRGB JPEGs; SHA-256 in frame order: 3102 548ed5766747ce264b0e5d88e094233ae6265e6a388b2c8ed1e1520e74c573ac, 3103 661642b869ffcc98e9189dcf66024905b38e811f4de51dd8ecfbad6b6a382ae1, 3104 ae7196e461d1714b4619d2689820b33fa3f23a87ed18cc718f1feec1056b9c39, 3105 b0ace10c58d6df6da99c67de34cfd2c476b43a51c5c83c95abbfc8aa0fa9d610, 3106 9f3d626a1763de1698bd0c623204b8c10108d7eaf8b58fdeadabb6435bcbe5bc, 3107 2473c2aaa1a2d822c180eff66e4cfa0c555058d805017642e7cfdbc3af98da08, 3108 250c22d2f7c2eb468f7d1811a90b9bf66c2bf7f162f298d12b3daab5db74c244, 3109 061429dfe3d12d6a3a353ef825a841d0f182c8b6259e5b4c694c566d96881bd2, 3110 24605cdbb72591f3a2b56b0d19029239b98748d512cfd820d522f674182c3551); their MakerNote film tags, read with exiftool, match the schedule, and ExposureTime 1/60, ISO 1600, FNumber 4.5, Saturation 0/normal, Sharpness Normal, NoiseReduction 0/normal and DynamicRangeSetting Manual are uniform. EXIF reads quality FINE on all nine and the frames are JPEG-only where other shots in the source directory (DSCF3094, DSCF3099) carry .RAF companions, so the owner's typed FINED is FINE. Same-mode repeat spread over nine pairs (1186 matched blocks): pooled dL* +0.001 +- 0.005 with pair means in [-0.085, +0.100]; dC* +0.026 +- 0.008 with pair range [-0.057, +0.079]; dh* -0.019 +- 0.015 with pair range [-0.236, +0.114]. Within-round cross-mode differences repeat across the three rounds within 0.08 L*, 0.15 C* and 0.22 degrees: PROVIA to Std about +1.04 L* and -8.6 C*, PROVIA to Hi about -1.18 L* and -2.37 C*, Std to Hi about -2.15 L* and +6.24 C*. The weakest effect clears by about 6 combined standard errors, and the chroma and hue effects are 29x and 4x the same-mode envelope; the same-mode spread includes per-shot AF acquisition (frame drift reaches about 5 px) and the dL* triples close under composition, so the verdict is conservative in the same direction. Per-frame sharpness shows no soft frame (within-mode gradA agrees to 2 percent; the between-mode gradA offset tracks tone curves, not focus). External reference: the same method on six X-E1 reference images from fujivsfuji.com film-simulation-modes-compared (writeup private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/render-repeat-9/reference/report.md with the images and their SHA-256; Angry Birds 1780x717 and bookcase 2500x1217, grid adapted to keep the ~204x197 block size, NCC >= 0.95, C* subsets frozen, pixel-aligned seeds 0,0) gives Angry Birds (13-14 of 14 matched): Std-Provia dC* -4.51 +- 0.81, Hi-Provia dC* -1.32 +- 0.60, Hi-Std dL* -0.70 +- 0.13 and dC* +3.54 +- 0.62. Bookcase (34-38 of 40): Std-Provia dC* -1.38 +- 0.27, Hi-Provia dC* -0.78 +- 0.19 and dL* -2.25 +- 0.43, Hi-Std dL* -2.20 +- 0.36 and dC* +0.79 +- 0.18. The three ordering claims transfer from the X-E1 reference to the X-M1 nine shots in both reference sets: Std is the least saturated of the three, Hi sits between Std and Provia in saturation, and Hi is darker than Std (reference -0.70 to -2.20 L* against our -2.15), with hue signs agreeing. One sign does not transfer: Std versus Provia luma is +1.04 on the X-M1 but -0.16 +- 0.18 and -0.11 +- 0.13 in the references, both consistent with zero. The firmware-side reading of these measurements is E-FILMSIM-PRODUCERS-MMIO-150.
