limitations: Block medians, not per-pixel transfer curves: the differences are scene-relative level shifts at matched content, not the tone curve itself.

A global lighting change cannot be separated from a uniform render brightness change; the level-resolved pattern, the uniform sign across frame halves and the triangle consistency are the guard, and lighting constancy in the repeat run is owner-reported.
Parallax beyond the per-block rigid offset survives as residual mismatch in textured blocks; flat blocks (|grad L| <= 0.013) are used for the level-resolved reading.
Hue is only read where C* >= 8; hue changes of a few degrees near neutral are not measurable this way.
One body and one firmware state, two scenes with one run each; no per-pixel, other-scene or other-body claim beyond the X-E1 sign and ordering check.
The repeat run's flat subset is 3-7 blocks per pair, pooled only under the n >= 10 rule.
The repeat spread includes per-shot AF variation by design, so it mixes render and AF variability, and no fixed lens position is claimed.

The RenderCompare.hs on disk (SHA-256 bae333da...) does not match the version pinned for the triple (19ffd050...); the repeat analysis used the on-disk tool unmodified, and a latent align readout crash on negative fine offsets does not touch pair/pairsum.

The X-E1 reference transfers sign and ordering only: different bodies, scenes and lenses, WEBP CDN recompressions, small Angry Birds matched counts with an empty flat subset, and a bookcase hue triangle off 2.6 degrees against about 2.9 degrees combined errors.

label: static-inference
claim: On X-M1 1.50 the ROM's boot mode is selected only by two strap fields sampled once at reset, the ROM has no application-validity fallback, and nothing in the decoded software sets the selector (static-inference over byte-read ROM, record and image bytes; reports/sd-boot-claim-test.md, reports/recovery-hardware-routes.md sections 1.5, 1.6 and 5). The mode detect 0x80000260, called from 0x80000130, reads 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 at 0x80000274 and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 at 0x80000278, derives the mode at 0x8000027c-0x80000300 and writes the combined word back at 0x800002f0 with bits 2:0 preserved; the pre-detect path from 0x80000028 touches only MMIO 0xfff89008 and 0xfff88084 and SRAM, so the selection precedes every media, card, key and application access. Mode table: the chain 0x80000288-0x80000290 (mov r0,#7; bics r0,r0,r1; mvneq r0,#0) sets the zero flag iff r1 & 7 == 7, so any low selector 7 halts whatever bits 4:3 read; mode 1 (SD/FAT channel 0, dispatch 0x8000014c) needs the high pair 0b00 with low selector 0-6; mode 2 (raw channel 1, dispatch 0x80000164) needs low selector 4 with a nonzero high pair; mode 0 is reached only through low selector 6 with a nonzero high pair. This body presents high pair 3 and low selector 1 and boots mode 4 (E-STRAP-READ-150). Thirty-two executions of the unchanged mode-detect bytes under the Cortex-R5F proxy cover every low-selector and pair combination and return this table with the expected combined-word writeback (emulated); with selector 1 only modes 1 and 4 occur. Thirty-two prefix cases stop at 0x80000288 after both reads and the OR, with r1 = selector | (pair << 3), complete provenance and only the GPIO-setup store, before the writeback and dispatch: the boundary at which a conditional early-debug guard could permit only r1 values 01, 09, 11 and 19 and so exclude mode 2. The X70 harness test ../x70view/native/tests/test_driver_harness_api2.py RomImageTests executes the real 0x80000260 and returns -1 for low selector 7 on every high pair. The dispatch calls one handler per boot and halts at 0x80000020 on any nonzero return (0x800001f8-0x800001fc), and the call sites of 0x8000082c, 0x8000071c and 0x80000938 are the dispatch entries only. The ROM validates no staged record: mode 1 stages the directory-declared ffboot.bin to 0x40000000 and hands off to RAM 0 with no header, checksum, version or size check, and the mode 3-6 handler stages page groups after the marker scan with no checksum. Every handler failure returns -1 after clearing 0xfff88084 bit 0 (mode 1 0x80000858-0x80000860, mode 2 0x80000750-0x80000758, mode 3-6 0x80000978-0x80000984 and 0x80000a58-0x80000a60), so a damaged internal-media application produces a dark halt and not an SD boot. The record side matches: record 1's trailer gate 0x1cc0 and its storage, segment and decompressor failures call the teardown 0x1de8 and self-loop (0x1f18, 0x1f58, 0x1f90, 0x1fd8, 0x226c, 0x3d28), with no branch to the SD handlers, the ROM or a reset, and record 2 continues past its companion check instead of selecting another application. Selector writers: strap-read-safety.md section 3 finds no store to 0xfff89014 in any artifact and no access to 0xfff98000 outside the ROM, whose fixed stores preserve bits 2:0; a movw/movt pass over the ROM, both records, both loaders, images 4 and 5 and the plain image materializes 0xfff98000 nowhere and 0xfff89014 only as the port-mirror loop base (boot-40048.bin 0x2688, boot-50048.bin 0x22b8, id5-00bf1a00.bin 0x2d63ac), and the ROM rewrites 0xfff89008 before every sample. Computed access: FUN_006a0888 forms GPIO input addresses as 0xfff89000+((operand>>16)&15)*0x40+0x14, including application rows that read the ROM high pair; FUN_00656ff4/FUN_00741a00, FUN_007416c8 and FUN_00dba85c also compute port input addresses, the last reaching 0xfff89014 through its accepted bank 0; the sub-command rotation descriptors at 0x007cb1e4 select port 3 bits 8/9 while their direct bit-10 gate reads port 0; neighbouring computed GPIO writers target control and output offsets, not +0x14. The arbitrary-address service reader/writer FUN_00647b1c/FUN_00647b78 and the ROM config address/value stores can issue accesses to either strap target, which is not a readback showing any input bit writable. No consumer of the ten-base MMIO table 0x00829144-0x00829168 (holding 0xfff89000 and 0xfff98000) is found by the full decompiler export or by an aligned-pointer and paired movw/movt census across all eight artifacts. strap-scan.c's literal-load recognition does not require Rn=pc and produces false positives: the alleged GPIO copy loads at 0x6c9344, 0x6c9788, 0x6df9e0 and 0x6dddb4 read other peripheral blocks, so the constant-address census cannot support exhaustive absence or exact access counts, and no mapped computed store restores the withdrawn writable-low-selector claim. Consequence for the reported SD-boot unbrick practice (reported: boot working firmware from the SD card instead of broken firmware, then update through the normal process): no card property read by the main CPU can set the mode (an effect of the card outside the main CPU is unexplained and open, E-SDBOOT-CARD-ACTUATION-CONTRAST-150), no earlier boot can hand a selector down and no validity check exists to fall back from, so a broken application cannot cause an SD boot; SD boot needs the strap fields to read SD values at the reset sample, which on this body happens with Fn plus the inward sub-command-dial press under fast power toggling (E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150). A mode-1 card restores nothing by itself: the ROM stages one file and supplies no media writer, so a recovery card carries its own chain in ffboot.bin.
scope: XM1-body-01 official 1.50; the captured 16 KiB boot-ROM artifact, both boot records, both loaders, decoded images 4 and 5, the plain image, the full recovered decompiler export and the existing reviewed captures; bounded Cortex-R5F proxy execution of the unchanged mode-detect bytes with fixture inputs that model software decision values, not hardware reset provenance (native wire inputs and reports under private-data/scratch/selector-decision). Host-only: no camera or USB access, no card written, no selector write, no payload executed.
commands: llvm-objdump over the wrapped 16 KiB artifact, addresses 0x80000260-0x80000300

Full-export host search for direct, scaled-GPIO and selector-equivalent constants; aligned pointer and paired A32 movw/movt census into [0x00829100,0x0082916c) over ROM, both records, both loaders and images 4/5/plain
limitations: Both selector-writer checks are bounded negative evidence: the strap census omits register-offset, base-through-memory and table-driven forms, and the movw/movt pass sees only movw/movt pairs, so literal-pool constants, indirect writers and arbitrary-pointer or unrecognized code are not excluded; the unresolved MMIO base table is not proof of dead data or electrical immutability.

The electrical source and the warm-reset retention of 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 are unproved; SELECTOR-WRITE-01 and RESET-RETENTION-01 stay open (E-SD-BOOT-FORCING-BACKBURNER-150).

Software bus-store requests do not establish low-bit writeability, pad electrical influence or reset retention; no changed-selector readback is held and the service writer is not a proposed camera operation.

The early-debug guard is a conditional design, not a built or verified camera operation; target debug availability, the actual execution alias and reset or pin effects are unverified, and an operational guard would not replace the mode-1 configuration and payload byte review.
The practice's second half (update through the normal process) runs under the application and does not bear on the ROM selection.

Private input/capture paths and local agent/run artifacts are historical provenance, unavailable in the public checkout. Public report sources describe findings; existing artifact hashes identify historical versions and were not recomputed during publication.

label: emulated
claim: Host spike against the pinned nixpkgs Unicorn 2.1 engine, synthetic instruction words only, no X-M1 code (one run, 2026-10-09; throwaway program outside the repo, command below). Results: no Cortex-R4 or R4F model exists in the uc_cpu_arm enum (R5F is the only R-profile model); mrc p14,0,rX,c2,c0,0 ends emulation with UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID under UC_CPU_ARM_CORTEX_R5F and also with no model selected, its c0 form fails under R5F, and the mcr p14 write form fails under R5F, so the boot records' per-core discriminator (firmware-extraction.md CPU profile) cannot execute unmodified; mrc p15,0,r0,c0,c0,0 returns 0x411fc153 (the R5F MIDR), mrc p15 c1 returns 0, mrc p15 c2 is UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID, mrc p15 c13 returns 0, and mrc p15,0,r0,c0,c1,0 (CTR) returns UC_ERR_OK without writing r0; svc #0 reports interrupt 2 to UC_HOOK_INTR, advances the PC and takes no vector or mode switch; msr cpsr_c,#0x13 changes CPSR; wfi executes as a no-op; mcr p15 c6 (MPU) and mrc/mcr p15 c7 (cache) execute as no-ops. Consequence: a full-system model on this engine implements exception entry and return, the discriminator substitute, MPU/cache semantics and every device in the harness.
scope: One host run of a throwaway C program against the build's pinned Unicorn 2.1 (libunicorn.so.2 from the bazel external lab_unicorn repository), UC_ARCH_ARM, UC_MODE_ARM|LITTLE_ENDIAN, cases of 2 to 4 synthetic instructions on a private page, run from the engine's default SVC-mode reset state (CPSR 0x400001d3, I and F set); no project code, fixture, camera or device access.
limitations: Synthetic words only; says nothing about X-M1 silicon, timing or engine behaviour on real code.
One engine version and build; a different pin could change any row.
The p14 tests cover read and write of one register address; other debug registers were not enumerated.

label: static-inference
claim: Assessment of what a full-system emulation of this body would take, from the project's bounded runner (reports/full-system-emulation.md). Distance: components the project can build from held bytes are the boot path, decompression, the internal-media read path, DMA/fill-copy (the 0xfff02000 register map still undecoded), the interrupt controller (0xfff01000, decode pending), timers, the second CPU and the SD path; components that lack information are media physics (spare/window semantics, bad-mark persistence, erase/program behaviour, the +0x404 owner, the technology name), the display/GPU block, the sensor and lens, and the per-core task assignment. Two-CPU verdict: the second CPU is a boot rendezvous requirement, because record 1 waits on the peer cells 0x40020000/0x40020004 while record 2 clears its own (both byte-read), so a single-engine model needs a declared peer substitute for record 2's three writes and handoff; at runtime the only task whose kernel is identified, mujin, sits under loader A's kernel (0x4005476c/0x40054770 pair) and no mapped evidence assigns a task or the menu/develop paths to loader B's kernel, so a single-kernel model is testable and an added second engine is a bounded later step. Bootrom value: executing the body's own 16 KiB block makes a divergence a device-model bug rather than a decode question and supplies the poll obligations any model must satisfy. Smallest useful target: T1, the real ROM mode 4 through both records, the loaders and decompressed image 4 to loader A's entry, accepted by comparison with the captured dump over the pinned extents; T2 adds the kernel and image 4's own loaders; T3 adds the menu and develop path and is several person-months because its device surface is only partly mapped. Recommendation: do not build now; make the bounded collaboration ask to the two reporters first, and build T1 only when an experiment names the expansion per spec/03.
scope: Host assessment over the named reports and bytes, the engine spike E-EMUL-ENGINE-SPIKE-150 and the reported leads recorded in E-X70-REFERENCE-ASSESS-150; cost figures are unmeasured estimates.
sources: docs/evidence.jsonl E-DUMP-RAM-150, E-RAM-PROBE-150, E-LZ-ENCODER-150, E-STRAP-READ-150, E-SDBOOT-CARD-IMAGE-150, E-SD-BOOT-ENTRY-HOLD-150
limitations: No component was built or timed; the cost figures are estimates with no measured part.
The device list is bounded by what the project's reports have decoded; an unlisted peripheral could add a component.
No simulator result accepts a gate, changes the recovery position or authorizes a flash.
E-X70-REFERENCE-ASSESS-150 replaces the recommendation's collaboration ask with a concrete one now that the X70 emulator is readable, and E-T1-BUILD-PLAN-150 holds the T1 plan.

claim: Block-by-block comparison of the X70 emulator's hardware models (X70-reported) against our own body's bytes, for the blocks the previous full-system assessment named (reports/x70-emulator-reference.md section 3.2). Our side is a fresh constant-address access scan with private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/strap-scan.c over our ROM, both boot records, both loaders, images 4 and 5 and the plain image for ranges 0xfffb3000, 0xfffb4000, 0xfff01000, 0xfff91000 and 0xfff52000, plus the decodes in reports/bootrom-window.md and reports/firmware-extraction.md; the scanner decodes movw/movt, mov/mvn and pc-relative literal bases with immediate offsets and skips register-offset, post-indexed and table-driven forms, so the census is a lower bound. Readings: clock 0xfff88000 agrees (their ready bits 28-request to 24-ready and the +0x80 bit 16 status with our ROM's waits at 0xfff88080 bit 16, 0xfff88038 bit 28 to bit 24, and 0xfff88084 bit 0 on the halt path); GPIO 0xfff89000 agrees on the 0x40-stride port layout and on port 0 bits 11:10 as the boot source, which their boot fixture also sets; system 0xfff98000 agrees on the same five offsets {0,8,0x100,0x104,0x208}; DRAM 0xfff99000 is their DRAM controller and our unidentified block, with our config writes at +0x04..+0xf8, polls at +0x04/+0x08 and read-modify-write at +0x1c inside their offset set; reset 0xfffb2000 agrees on the same five offsets {4,8,0xc,0x10,0x14} that our ROM's every-boot pair writes hit; PHY 0xfff01000 agrees on the start bit at +0x00 and ready at +0x90 bit 28 and on the 0x248-wide register window our ROM indexes, so that base is not an interrupt controller; the two interrupt banks at 0xfffb3000/0xfffb4000 accept our ROM's conditional config words at +0x8c/+0xac/+0x10c/+0x12c/+0x15c, both records' +0xc00 writes, boot record 1's bit-24 writes to bank-1 +0x8c/+0xac/+0xcc/+0xec and image 5's enable read-modify-writes at +0x80..+0x8c/+0xa0..+0xac; timers 0xfff91000 agree on the register triple 0/4/8 that both records, both loaders and image 4 use, with our reload 30000, the counter/1875 tick measured at 99.88 Hz and the callback id 32 against their inferred power-of-two divider 1<<((control>>4)&7) and unmeasured physical source; the decompressor 0xfff43000 agrees on start +0x04, source +0x40, length +0x44, destination +0x48, read-only output count +0x4c, acknowledge +0x88, 16 KiB job pages and the 20-byte stream header before the token stream our decoder also skips; the media controller 0xfff52000/0xfff52800 agrees on type-1 geometry (2 KiB page, 64 pages per 128 KiB block), the 512-byte aperture at +0x400 whose first 16 bytes their program model fills from registers 0x40-0x4c (a candidate reading for our spare-prefix question and the unnamed +0x404 accept field), done and acknowledge at +0x54, and the DMA words +0xa0 (tag 0x401000), +0xa4 and +0xa8. Their 0xfff02000 fill/copy model supplies a register set where our assessment listed the map as missing. Coverage gaps that are not conflicts: our interrupt-bank reads at offsets 0x00..0x0c sit outside the families their model accepts, and each X70 model's register set is its own firmware's observed accesses. Classification: no evidence of a different chip, no evidence either way on revision, and the remaining differences are the same chip used by different firmware with different peripherals and a config block that skips the 0xfffb3000 sequence on our body (field +0x54 = 0x001a0000). Sibling-derived readings for our own labels, each unproved on our body until our own decode or a capture settles it: (1) 0xfff01000 is a PHY-class block, not the interrupt controller: our ROM writes bit 0 to +0x00, writes 146 indexed words over +0x00..+0x248 and then waits unbounded on 0xfff01090 bit 28, and the state snapshot in image 5 at 0xed43dc reads bank offsets through 0x306c, while the X70 model's only semantics for that base are a start bit at +0x00 and a ready bit at +0x90 bit 28. (2) The two 128-source interrupt-controller banks are 0xfffb3000 and 0xfffb4000, whose families hold every access listed above, including boot record 1's bit-24 writes at sites 0x1ec4-0x1ed0. (3) Record 1's write of 0x01000000 to bank-1 +0xcc is the second core's release: it is the register and value the X70 board watches (0xfffb40cc bit 24) to start CPU1 after its high vectors are copied, which matches our own finding that the second CPU's side of the boot rendezvous is small and scripted. (4) The 0x3fff00xx exception-vector literals in boot record 2, unexplained in reports/update-validation-and-boot.md, name the second core's high-vector region at 0x3fff0000 in the X70 board's CPU1 handling.
scope: Host-only static comparison of our artifacts against the X70 project's Python model code and comments; the X70 emulator was not built or run, no X70 artifact was executed and no X70 code was copied. Every reading taken from the X70 side is sibling-derived and not an X-M1 fact until our own bytes or a capture settle it.
limitations: The census covers constant-address instruction forms only; register-offset, post-indexed and table-driven accesses are outside it, so each our-bytes finding is a lower bound.
The X70 side is its model code and comments, not a datasheet or a measurement, and a model's offsets are its firmware's access set.
The X70 emulator was not executed for this row.

reports/bootrom-window.md section 4 still lists 0xfff01000 and 0xfffb3000 as unidentified blocks; the PHY-class and interrupt-bank readings above are the sibling-derived candidates for them.

claim: The image-5 record rebuild is built and its stock reproduction is proven (byte-read geometry and code; host runs of //host/firmware:rebuild-update). extract-record5 writes the pinned container's record 5 in record-file form and replace-record5 substitutes a record with the record-4 gate chain, sliding the stream inside the record's own flash window so every media offset beyond the new record keeps its stock byte. Geometry: segment entry {5, 0x00bf1a00, 0x004f1e60, 0x01460000, 0x002bbe40, 0x002c0000, 0x002e0000, 0x20, 1}; record at media 0x2c0000, 20-byte header, stream 0x2c66bd; window [0x2c0000, 0x5a0000) = flash + flash_length, 96 per cent used, the remaining 0x1992f bytes uniform file 0xff. The window may not end past the nearest segment region above the record, the lowest stored flash base above the window start among the other entries: entry 6's 0x5a0000, the plain image's first byte, 0x700000 below the image-2 extent at 0xca0000, which stays a second condition. A bound on the image-2 extent alone would let a source whose entry-5 flash_len is enlarged to 0x9e0000 pass every gate and a replacement stream cover the plain image's bytes [0x5a0000, 0xca0000), because the fit bound spans that interval and the carried-identity check compares against the same source. replaceRecord5 also refuses a replacement without an attached decoded image, one whose decoded-size word moves, a declared window that closes before the stock record, and a stream that does not fit it. The CLI fails closed on the record header arithmetic (the parser cuts the stream to word 1; assemblyChecks and the CLI total_len check enforce it), the shipped-record invariants, an fflzd record round trip, the emission gates, and a read-back of the written file (the five stored words against the record file's, the stream, the three checksums recomputed over the file's own ranges, carried identity outside the rebuilt record and the main checksum word, invariants and an fflzd round trip of the record the file carries), removing the output on failure. Host runs 2026-10-09, before and after the window fix: extract-record5 wrote the stock record (2,909,905 bytes, SHA-256 687a9bfbfd0383aeee134141ba715a5641c10db7e38d3b3c83768535e955c6ad) and replace-record5 fed it back unchanged and emitted a container byte-identical to the pinned file over all 38,405,148 bytes (SHA-256 43d67afa1a2bc9ae8481bc0acf02cb085ed0f515122dcbd26addcae102cd1490), reporting the input record and the rebuilt stream each passing fflzd round trips against the 5,185,120-byte decode, 0 differing stream bytes, 41/41 contract fields on the emitted container and 0 carried bytes differing outside the image-5 record and the main checksum word. //host/firmware:update-container-tests covers identity emission, short/long/exactly-filling streams with the window rule and the refusals; its long-stream and window-fill fixtures append bytes that differ from the stock pattern at every index. The E-RECIPE-D3-PATCH-150 limitation that the image-5 record operation is not built no longer holds.
scope: Host-only: the pinned official 1.50 DAT and its image-5 decode; no camera, USB device or media was touched. The emitted container equals the pinned file and is not an install candidate.
limitations: No modified-image record-5 container exists in this record: the D3 site patch at image-5 0x00d50a48 needs a patched decode and an encoder run before replace-record5 applies to it.
The window rule is byte placement and a source-word relation; what the loader or the engine does with the window slack remains unproved, as for record 4.

The window end is the record's declared flash length, which coincides with the plain image's flash base in the stock container; a container where they disagree, or whose stored flash words do not describe its layout, is refused rather than resolved.

No record-4 change was made: the record-4 slide is bounded by the parsed gap part up to the record-5 base, which is the layout scan's bound on this container, and the F1 harm needs an abutting region whose content the replacement can overwrite while the gates report identity; a doctored source that declares a region base inside the record-4 gap remains unrefused, as the chain leaves the source to the printed hash.

Record 1 (payload 0x40048, base 0, reset 0x1800; decode/ghidra/boot-40048.c FUN_00001800): sets 0x40020000 and 0x40020004 to 0x22b; copies 0x3e8 bytes from RAM 0x10000 to 0x7fff0000, the alias of physical 0x3fff0000; writes 0x01000000 to 0xfffb408c, 0xfffb40cc, 0xfffb40ac and 0xfffb40ec; initializes storage (FUN_00002034), builds the block skip list (FUN_00002058, 0x4804 = 0x4310), reads the segment table from media 0x140000 to 0x61c000 (FUN_00001dc4), publishes 0x4310 into 0x61c188, checks the trailer halfword at 0x24a0000 + 0x1e for 0xaaaa (FUN_00001cc0), copies loader records id 0/1 (FUN_0000231c) and decompresses image 4 with its bss fill (FUN_00002250, the fill over 0x89ec00 + 0x352e00 and then the engine to 0x61c400); FUN_00001d08 stores the loader record's header word at +0xc (0x40020) into RAM 0x4300 and *(0x61c40c) into 0x4304; the path clears 0x400a00c4, clears its own sync cell, waits for 0x40020004 to leave 0x22b, and the reset path's final transfer goes through 0x4300/0x4304 after the supervisor switch at 0x183c. Record 2 (payload 0x50048, base 0x10000, reset 0x11800; boot-50048-10000.c FUN_00011cc0): reads the boot-reason sample from companion register 0x6000 into 0x400a00c0, reads 16 one-byte companion values from 0x5000..0x5f00 into 0x400a00d0..0x400a00df and validates them (byte 14 = 0xaa, byte 15 = minus the sum of the first 15 bytes), writes 0x40020004 = 0, waits for 0x40020000 to leave 0x22b, and looks up shared segment id 1 for its handoff through 0x14c80/0x14c84. The kind-2 arm of FUN_006a0888 reads the word at (0x3ffe240 + (operand >> 16 & 0xf)) * 0x40 + 0x14, which is 0xfff89014 + bank*0x40, extracts bit operand & 0xf, and sets the row state to (halfword at row +0x12) == bit; both rows therefore assert while GPIO0 bit 11 (Fn) or bit 10 (dial push) reads 0. The act session bound the physical Fn press and the sub-command push to codes 0x28 and 0x2b (E-PRESS-MAP-150), and the idle jig capture reads bits 11:10 = 1 (E-STRAP-READ-150), the rows' unasserted level. Consequence for the entry question: the cardless sweep's Function-plus-sub-command-push run held both mapped controls at power-on and the ROM still sampled mode 4, so that negative is about the reset sample's value, not about pressing controls that never reach the bits; the run-time binding is established and the pads' reset-time electrical availability is the open question (reports/sd-boot-claim-test.md sections 3 and 5, E-SD-BOOT-FORCING-BACKBURNER-150). The MOVIE control, row 21, is analog ADC9 rather than GPIO0 bit 11. The held service manual identifies assemblies and the Fn and dial SD-card procedure, not a strap pinout or a separate service-card electrical interface.

claim: Upstream SD-boot reports (reported). x70view (X70) reaches the ROM's SD boot path by supplying the two strap inputs as board fixtures and holding the two console controls its own procedure names. Cited reads, host-only: emulator/boot_devices.py BootControls takes boot_source=1 (stored to 0xfff98000, the low selector) and boot_gpio=0xc00 (port 0 bits 11:10 high, the mode-4 pair with low 1), calls the straps and initial register values simulation fixtures in its limits, refuses writes to a port's input word, and leaves 0xfff98000 in its writable system set with no pre-sample writer; native/tests/test_driver_harness_api2.py RomImageTests executes the real 0x80000260 and asserts the mode table this project reads. emulator/sd_boot_board.py holds SD_BOOT_PINS = ((0,10),(0,11)) low at reset through set_gpio_input_pin, with the source description 'SD-boot buttons held at power-on', and releases them at the 0xfff98008 handoff, with a card present (GPIO12 bit 7 low) and a strict ROM-grammar SD host (emulator/rom_sd_boot.py); research/sd-boot.md records the case results: pins low with a card gives the mode-1 chain (154 sectors, 70,144 bytes DMA'd to 0x40000000, handoff value 2), the normal 0xc00 fixture gives the internal-media path with the card never read, and pins low with a missing ffsys.bin or no card halts with no NAND fallback. research/button-monitor/README.md names GPIO0/10 KEY_CMDL_PUSH and GPIO0/11 KEY_FUNCTION3, and research/sd-boot-card/README.md gives the modelled physical procedure (hold the rear command dial pressed in and the red record button while switching on; the ROM samples the two buttons only at power-on; a wrong card leaves a dark screen, marked untested on the camera). Their own note states the two-button strap derivation is static and has not been observed on hardware, and upstream never published how the X-E2 was made to select SD boot. The owner relayed the x70view author's advice on 2026-10-11 to hold FN3, physically the X70 red record button, and push the rear command dial to boot /ffsys.bin and /ffboot.bin from SD; the author said he plans to test firmware this way, so the advice is a plan, not a physical execution. tiredboffin (fffw) relayed through the owner that his working X-E2 ffboot was custom code that began as an LED blink and became a programmer loading a standard DAT from FAT SD and flashing EEPROM; NAND/DMA, secondary-CPU neutralization and bad-block management remain partly understood even there, and building ffboot from DAT firmware (X-T4) is his current development work, not a published renamed-DAT or full-application SD-boot recipe. What transfers: the shared ROM's arithmetic, mode table, file names and unvalidated handoff, and the normal-boot strap values, which match this body's live pair. Control identities do not transfer: bit 11 carries Fn on this body where the X70 binds its record button (E-SDBOOT-M1-PIN-BINDING-150), and the X70 fixture establishes the strap values the decode needs, not that physical controls reach the pads on either body.

claim: On pinned X-M1 1.50, property 0x1d is the file-type component of IMAGE QUALITY: 0 is JPEG only, 1 is RAW only, 2 is JPEG+RAW (static-inference over byte-read decompilation of the pinned decoded images; the act correspondence is hardware-observed). IMAGE QUALITY's five menu rows are a product of two fields and both commit paths state the product: settings case 0xfa of FUN_00d4fc74 splits each row into a FINE/NORMAL cell 0x00956890 and a 0x1d cell 0x0095689c (rows FINE and NORMAL take 0x1d 0, FINE+RAW and NORMAL+RAW take 2, RAW takes 1), and FUN_006441c0 composes property 0xfa back from the same two cells, one 0xfa code per pair, with 0x1d 1 giving RAW whatever the FINE/NORMAL cell reads. The 0x1d cell is filled by availability walk FUN_0063eb60 and consumed by FUN_00d13c38, the RAW action (the Fn assignable list names RAW at col0 3, and 00d40770 re-syncs the quality cell whenever one of 0xfc, 0xfd or 0x1bc..0x1c1 reads 3), by FUN_006427bc and FUN_006434f8 at rebuild, and by FUN_00d4d6b4 on the default refresh. The ordinary field is payload p+070 bits 5-6 (record +0x98, getter offset +0x80 from the bank base), custom record +0x06 bits 6-7. Act 1 of the ten-act session, IMAGE QUALITY FINE to FINE+RAW, therefore moves p+036 and p+070 in one commit with codes 0 to 2 in both (hardware-observed, E-SETTINGS-ACTS-150), and the earlier 47-record window shows p+070 moving in exactly the five pairs where p+036 moves, always 0/2.

label: static-inference
claim: On pinned X-M1 1.50, property 0x161 is the exposure-mode memory of which value family last committed through the settings path: 1 for the IMAGE SIZE family (image size 0xf6, movie image size 0xf2), 2 for the ISO family (ISO 0x141, AUTO-ISO maximum 0x14f), 0 for the getter default branch (static-inference over byte-read decompilation; the act correspondence is hardware-observed). FUN_00641438 is the post-commit display update most settings cases of FUN_00d4fc74 call after their FUN_0063c51c(0x34,0,prop) notification, carrying a family id per property (image size 1, ISO 2, film simulation 3, dynamic range 4, colour 5, sharpness 7, tone 8, bracketing 9, focus mode 0xd, image quality 0xe, face detection 0xf); it writes 0x161 only when that id is 1 or 2 and the shooting-mode cell 0x00956838 reads 0x21..0x25, and writes the sibling 0x165 instead in mode 0x1f. FUN_00646958 reads the property back at UI-session init FUN_00637478 and after the shooting reset FUN_00d46d10; FUN_006373f4 and FUN_006376a0 hold the per-mode RAM cells 0x009518f8..0x00951904; FUN_0063c51c consults the cell inside the size-line and ISO-line change branches. The ordinary field is payload p+05e bits 5-6 (record +0x86, getter offset +0x6e), custom record +0x25 bits 6-7. Act 9 of the ten-act session, ISO 200 to 6400, is the only act that moves it, a9 to c9, codes 1 to 2, because the ISO case passes family id 2, while act 1 passes 0xe, act 2 passes 4, acts 3, 7 and 8 reach cases that call no FUN_00641438 at all, act 4 passes 8, act 5 passes 5, act 6 passes 7 and act 10 passes 0xd (hardware-observed, E-SETTINGS-ACTS-150). The 47-record window agrees: all seven defaults writes return the code to 0, the six saves carrying the owner size/aspect state hold code 1 beside p+06d, and the single pair moving ISO p+042 holds code 2.
scope: X-M1 1.50 image-4 and image-5 decompilation over the pinned decoded images, cross-checked against the 2026-10-09 area-2 captures; host-only, no camera was enumerated, opened or commanded in this pass.
limitations: What the remembered family changes for the user is unproved: no menu node carries 0x161, and the mapped readers reach only the change bookkeeping and the display rebuild.

label: hardware-observed
claim: The first bank erase the project has captured is in the owner-run install-day read 20261009T163721Z-read-media, with 20261009T072111Z-read-media as the before image (hardware-observed; reports/settings-byte-map-150.md section 2.1). Before: bank 0 slots 0..30 hold sequences 0x239a..0x23b8 and bank 1 slots 0..30 hold 0x23b9..0x23d7, 62 of 62 slots occupied. After: bank 0 slot 0 holds 0x23d8, slots 1..30 and the whole tail past slot 30 are erased to ff, and bank 1 is byte-identical to the before image (SHA-256 23d7a3882318bcc6964facbe0b6e6395a1c2ffb88e9ba4f859f8c6e4c944efc9 both times). Exactly one commit lies between the captures: sequence 0x23d8 = 0x23d7 + 1, a save whose 0x118 body equals 0x23d7 apart from counter byte r+026 15 to 16 and the DCF path digits DSCF3092 to DSCF3094, with both parity regions recomputed. The erase took the older generation 0x239a..0x23b8 and nothing else, 31 records; the ten act records, boundary record 0x23cd and the five pre-boundary records survive in bank 1. The outcome matches the mapped area-2 append chain step for step (byte-read, area2-invalidation.md section 4.2): 0x006a8074 commits only on a difference, 0x006ac7d4 stamps newest+1 and tries 0x006ad3f4 in the newest record bank, switches bank on an append failure, retries there, and only after a second failure calls 0x006ad51c to erase the bank it switched to before retrying, so the victim is the older generation. The capacity arithmetic the session scripts use is confirmed and unchanged: free counts the appends before the next erase, and this erase struck on the first append after free reached 0; what the observation adds is that one commit-on-difference prices one slot whatever produced it, so the shot that yielded 0x23d8 cost a slot like any menu edit, and that a wrap destroys one generation of up to 31 records, so a capture holds at most two generations.

label: emulated
claim: The editable bank stores its seven slots on the SD card, which makes a writable card a dependency; the backend choice is the design's and is not an owner decision on record (reports/named-recipe-reach.md section 6, reports/recipe-design.md section 18.3). The bank lives in two files, RECIPEA.BIN and RECIPEB.BIN. Format 1 (static-inference design) is 512 bytes per file: a 32-byte typed header (magic FJRB, format 1, firmware tag 150, slot count 7, name units 12, payload 0x28, generation, blob length 462, complement-sum checksum over the blob, slot-valid mask) followed by the 462-byte blob of 7 payloads then 7 names. The current format is the typed 1024-byte v2 bank in the host codec and the firmware storage ABI (emulated): it persists selection, auto-update policy, optional ordinary base, populated names and distinct saved/working payloads. Safe v1 generations migrate in RAM with working=saved, NOTHING SELECTED, DISABLE and an invalid base, preserving the original file until a verified v2 write to the nonwinner. Load precedence is the valid file with the higher generation, ties to A; cross-version generation ordering keeps A-on-tie and refuses a newest semantically unsafe generation without falling back to an older one or rewriting either file. A write targets the file not holding the current bank and is read back and revalidated after close, with no retries and whole-file validation before any apply; generation wrap is refused before any truncate. Format-1 validation covers the complete walked record (81 fields in that design) against its conversion tables where the table resolves, the names, the exact file length with zero trailing padding and a checksum over the whole file with the checksum field zeroed, so generation and the slot mask are integrity-checked. The status domain is a typed enum 0..12 with 0..8 plus 10/11 caller-visible. Save Current and Recall are whole-record operations over the 0x28 payload through the bank's own record walk, not FUN_00630b14 (E-RECIPE-BANK-FILEABI-150), against the inert scratch record, bank-0 row 2 at 0x0096cdf4; stock C and area 3 are never written and C-position recall keeps the stock edit volatility (E-CPOS-EDIT-VOLATILITY-150). The payload's +0x00/+0x02 halfwords are bound properties 0x1cb/0x1cc (getter arms 0x623198/0x623130, null table pointers at 0x81b7c8/0x81b7cc), leaving only +0x27 bits 3-7 unbound. The internal multi-custom remnant gives no persistence: the area-3 boot path 0x006a8abc restores one record to mirror offset 0x140 = slot 0 only. claim: The bounded native runner admits the A32 forms that the pinned artifacts execute and the target ISA defines, and keeps an exclusion only where CPU-profile evidence backs it; the A32 divide family is that remaining exclusion, and unprivileged load/store forms (LDRT/STRT/LDRBT/STRBT, LDRHT/STRHT) stay refused across widths until admitted with their own fixtures. The admitted set was widened in five artifact-driven rounds on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 and is verified by fixture runs (E-RECIPE-KERNEL-ACCEPT-150). In the halfword/bitfield, doubleword, dispatch and register-offset rounds every fixture word was checked with clang --target=armv7r-none-eabi plus llvm-mc or llvm-objdump, and corpus scans over the case manifests found no existing expectation that flips. Tail transfers: an ARM unconditional B to a declared function outside the current function is a tail transfer, and every other out-of-function target is left to the engine so the target fetch runs its checks in order (nonexec or unmapped gives fetch_guard, then four-byte containment gives unknown_call). Fixtures pin fetch-permission (fetch_guard pc 0x00002004), fetch-page-gap and fetch-cross-boundary (fetch_guard pc 0x00001008), tail-undeclared (B from 0x1004 to 0x1008, unknown_call pc 0x00001008), tail-outside (fetch_guard pc 0x00002000) and tail-transfer (returned, r0 7, r1 0x12, pc 0x1080). BX Rm to a declared A32 function is admitted through the same tail-transfer path and the BX LR return is unchanged; a Thumb target (bit 0), Rm=R15, or a non-LR register target with target&3 != 0 is refused unsupported_instruction before execution, because ARMv7-R leaves the misaligned PC write unpredictable (unsupported-bx-unaligned: target 0x1006, pc 0x1008, r12 0x1006); an unmapped or non-exec target gives fetch_guard and a mapped executable target outside every declared function gives unknown_call. Halfword and bitfield: post-indexed immediate LDRH/STRH (P=0 W=0, access at the base, base updated by plus or minus imm8, a base-update carry refused as memory_guard, destination equal to base refused) and SBFX/BFI/BFC alongside UBFX are admitted; field-inverted inserts (e7c40411 disassembles as bfi r0,r1,#4,#1), unallocated bitfield siblings and PC operands are refused at the instruction, and no word is admitted as BFXIL, which the clang armv7r-none-eabi assembler rejects for A32. This makes the compiled hook walk at 0x0061c3d8 and the stock setter bfi at 0x00629438 (940 sites) executable (source-inspected). Doubleword: LDRD/STRD pre-indexed with an immediate offset, writeback optional when the base is not one of the two transferred registers, Rt even with Rt+1 below the PC, both words preflighted separately and a 32-bit address carry refused as memory_guard; register-offset and post-indexed variants, odd Rt, the PC-base literal form, a pair containing the PC and writeback with the base in the pair (CONSTRAINED UNPREDICTABLE) are refused, the last two explicitly because llvm-objdump does not decode those words. The exclusion was lifted on artifact evidence (source-inspected): the frozen storage kernel's -Oz code has strd r8,[sp] e1cd80f0 at 0x011de5dc. Register-base load-to-PC dispatch: ldr pc,[Rn,Rm{,shift}] with Rn and Rm not the PC, pre-indexed, no writeback, word, immediate LSL/LSR/ASR; the entry read is preflighted as a word and target containment stays the code hook's property; PC base or index, writeback and the byte and store forms to the PC are refused, and an entry outside the declared function refuses at the target fetch as unknown_call. Site (source-inspected): e791f100 (ldr pc,[r1,r0,lsl#2]) at 0x011de670 in rb_map_completion. Register-offset writeback: byte and word transfers pre-indexed with immediate LSL/LSR/ASR, writeback optional, no PC operand and no load whose writeback base is its own destination; the halfword register-offset form also takes writeback, with bits 11-8 still required zero. Refused at the instruction: post-indexed register-offset forms including the unprivileged P=0 W=1 sibling (llvm-mc decodes it as LDRT), register-specified shifts and bit-4 scratch words, ROR, PC operands and loads with writeback into the same register, word and halfword (CONSTRAINED UNPREDICTABLE; llvm-mc marks them as potentially undefined encodings). Sites in the kernel slice (source-inspected): ldrb r3,[r1,-r2,lsl#1]! at 0x11dd770 (e7713082, r1 0x011dee7c, r2 0xffffffff), ldrb r4,[r2,r4]! at 0x11ddfd0 (e7f24004), ldrb r2,[r0,r2]! at 0x11de06c (e7f02002), and halfword e1b150b0 at 0x11dddcc, e1b150b6 at 0x11ddd50 and e1b500b4 at 0x11dd698. U=0 address computations subtract modulo 2^32 and range-check the result across the register-offset, immediate byte/word, halfword and doubleword forms, so the 0x11dd770 access resolves to the mapped 0x011dee7e and register-offset-subtract-guard (e7520003) wraps to 0xffff2004 outside every region as memory_guard; the U=1 carry refusal is unchanged and pinned by register-offset-byte-guard. After the last round the kernel's remaining refusal-class words inside declared functions are address-like literal-pool constants only (source-inspected), and a later stop is a scan defect fixed against the case's evidence, not a new admission decision. The storage kernel validates a 512-byte bank file by summing the whole file with the four checksum bytes at +0x18 zeroed and included (source-inspected); emulation/RecipeBankCases.hs encodes files the same way.

label: source-inspected
claim: The boot publication redesign is source-complete. It uses a 32-byte header, fixed-offset metadata (16-slot allowlist at image offset 0, 64-slot publication table at 0x80, name table at 0x9d84), an image_bytes minimum covering the metadata and name table inside the hashed image, a rotate-add word hash (the 33-multiplier was rejected for its linear two-word compensation family), two-pass transactional publication with per-entry allowlist destination checks and a region-bounded scan, and a failure path that stores nothing. A four-byte package fails the covered-length gate before any store, the store-at-zero case is unreachable because zero is the terminator and lies in no window, permutations are not preserved by the hash and single-word changes are always detected. The hash has one deterministic compensating-collision class: words a multiple of 32 positions apart with zero-sum changes cancel in carry-free stretches because rotation by 7 has order 32; the reachable case is zero-filled stretches, such as unused publication slots, with two words set to 0x80000000; outside those stretches carries perturb the pair in about one in six random contexts, and distances that are not multiples of 32 do not cancel. The class is named as a residual rather than closed because the four runs have no spare byte. The first redesign measured entry 48 of 48, check 96 of 96, sum 48 of 48 and publish 160 against its 96-byte run, 352 bytes against the 288-byte four-run home and 64 bytes short. The byte-source ruling was to consolidate the walks and hash pass first; consolidation did not close the deficit (loop sharing 164 bytes, worse than the two loops; a stub-only two-pass 156 bytes, still 60 over), so the ruling's trust-model route was taken: the store pass and the bulk cache pass are image code, 15 instructions at image offset 0x280, executed from the hashed source copy, and the counts now stand at 288 of 288 with all linker assertions passing. Validation was not trimmed. Review accepts that store-pass boundary conditionally under the named instruction-fetch coherence prerequisite, with the trusted path confirmed to hash before branching, validate the entire bounded table before the first store and never modify the source; the fixed metadata geometry, length gates, failure exit and four-run instruction counts agree with the linker assertions, and review of the collision-class correction is recorded in E-AUDIT-SOURCE-STATE-150. The redesign also fixed cache-helper calls that used numeric bl operands and a same-unit .set symbol, both of which assemble raw imm24 fields; they are now link-relocated through the .ld, and the six draft sections are rebalanced to the four runs.

The install wrote the container's image-4 word and its area-2 payload at flash 0x8ea5e0. The first ordinary boot with the photography card (no USB, 13:39 MDT) gave a black screen, no LED and no application start, unchanged after a minute or more, and a no-card boot after full power-off reproduced it, so the failure belongs to the installed image, not the card path; the verified bytes and the updater's completion screen make write corruption the less likely explanation. Its manifest patch-set.json (SHA-256 1bacef859e1999dbb59f3c958029f17d35da5d54280c9f91797f4064d294a8bd, input the installed RC0 decode a4d169bd961ec7df34e3b9b7108b624b79680c3cc50297e434e0b3607fb65551) yields decode id4-recorder.bin (2,632,196 bytes, SHA-256 241d75c014cd2cab94ff81755c96bf728dd9f3b67ae9b695b550a0f21c66c069), record4.bin (1,337,092 bytes, SHA-256 ac9510b707c993e8840123f1f2617c63d1ac229aaf9aaf6b963dfa26f15257c9) and container FWUP0002-recorder.DAT (38,405,148 bytes, SHA-256 e9f1ed59b21171a9227ea0f0fefd99c14160cf5b1c1ba53cc69c026e48429544). Its ten-case emulated runtime gate passed with no mismatches: Valid captured a 131,060-byte file equal to the synthetic store (journal cb 0x61c274, mode 1, tag 1, fifth argument 1, len 0x1fff4, src 0x400a0800); Short wrote 0x1000 then the remainder; Werr posted the close with error count 0 and kept first error 0xd; Werrpart copied error count 0x1000, dropped the remaining length by that count with the source unchanged and kept the error; Werrfull copied 0x1fff4 and left remaining 0; Openfail (declared failure 5) wrote no file; Zerohandle ended through the guard with no write or close; a type-0x72 record whose +4 word equals 0x13a52b03 did not fire while an appended type-0x0f record at slot 1 did; Noaf restored the receive argument every iteration with bounded stop 0xc0de; and Wrap, with wrapped next index 0, stopped early at 0xc0de. The per-job map covers 0xa0-0xac with 0xa3 and 0xab unbound and unclaimed. The Sol review's four findings against the redesign (E-AUDIT-SOURCE-STATE-150) are fixed: the scan-budget register is preserved across the attempt and search handlers, the deadline is gated on a caught-up scan, the overflow flags latch at detection, and the 40-byte version-2 trailer carries the attempt tick; the re-review returned correct with no findings after a wrap-count fix (E-AUDIT-SOURCE-STATE-150). label: static-inference
claim: What physically drives 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 (GPIO0 pads 10 and 11) and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 at the ROM's reset sample on XM1-body-01 is unidentified. Byte-read: the dispatch reads only those two fields, once, from 0x80000130 (ldr 0x80000274 and 0x80000278); the later stores (0x800002f0 preserving the sampled field shape, config apply touching only bits 17:16) do not overwrite a forced selection, so forced pads may be released after the sample. The pair is bound to Fn (bit 11) and the sub-command push (bit 10), active low (E-SDBOOT-M1-PIN-BINDING-150). The ROM proves one 32-bit store of 0x0c000c00 to GPIO0 +0x08 (0xfff89008) only; whether that store replaces or selectively sets bits, and the electrical function of +0x08 bits 11:10, are missing SoC facts, and the mask:level reading is a sibling-emulator convention, not X-M1 evidence. The cardless sweep (E-SD-BOOT-ENTRY-HOLD-150) excludes only high pair 0b00 under the tested holds; the captured value 3 is the idle condition taken with no mapped control held, and the same bits follow those controls at run time, so a single-control sample (0b01 or 0b10) stays possible. Card-present cold starts with Fn plus the dial press mostly stay dark, so their sample did not select mode 4, while entry occurs only under fast power toggling (E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150); neither identifies the nets or the low selector's source. Unproved: the availability and voltage of the two nets at the reset sample, package pins, intervening circuitry, any strap test pad, resistor or connector, and the physical source, writeability and reset retention of low selector bits 2:0. Direct pad forcing is staged in reports/sd-boot-forcing-sheet.md with an unpowered observation gate and one bounded attempt on the reviewed card, with electrical drive on unidentified nets as the named risk. The owner backburnered forcing on 2026-10-12 because the board access and electrical probing are too invasive for now, and reaffirmed that the physical Fn and sub-command-dial push controls work; act logging records both at application runtime (E-PRESS-MAP-150).
scope: Byte-read of the pinned boot ROM and image-4 rows, the held service material, prior hardware-observed input sessions and strap sweep, and the owner's priority decision. No probe, continuity measurement, board opening, card operation, camera attempt or electrical forcing occurred.
limitations: Application-runtime button operation does not establish reset-time strap sampling; both pins reading low at the ROM sample remains unobserved.

No target schematic or reset-domain documentation is held. Card contents are not an input to main-CPU selection, but an outside-main-CPU electrical effect of card presence is unproved rather than excluded (E-SDBOOT-CARD-ACTUATION-CONTRAST-150).

probe-straps reads the current maintenance boot's sample without issuing a reset, and its application transport cannot observe an SD or halt path that never reaches the application; a later reboot cannot recover an earlier reset sample. Adding UP, shutter S2 and USB to reach the maintenance gate is not physically equivalent to the SD actuation, and a standard-card measurement cannot assume selector 1 while mode 2 would consume raw sectors before transport exists. Host search closes at target documentation or a qualified early-debug hardware prerequisite.
Backburnering is a priority decision, not evidence that forcing would or would not work; the forcing sheet authorizes nothing, and board access needs an owner-discussed invasive plan.
A cold-start entry is not demonstrated and not proved physically impossible; the software writable-latch claim stays withdrawn.

label: static-inference
claim: The captured X-M1 mode-7 ROM path is a two-phase inbound receiver: it first receives exactly 1 KiB through the 0xfff56000 controller's +0x100 window and applies that block with the shared hardware-register interpreter, then clears the window-mode control bit and directly receives (config+0x18 & 0x3ffff) KiB at 0x40000000 before the shared RAM-0 handoff. It emits no transport request or response. Its register base and layout differ from the decoded application USB controller. Upstream fffw's BOOT_DEV56 is an unresolved address-derived enum name; published later Milbeaut USIO and SDHCI layouts are not direct matches. The known Fn/sub-command high pair can satisfy only the high selector and release condition; mode-7 entry still lacks low selector 5. No mode-7 image is deployable until endpoint, framing and producer are identified. The analysed input is the captured 16 KiB boot ROM bound in E-BOOTROM-PROBE-150 and E-BOOTROM-MODE4-150, not an update container. The development shell's LLVM 21.1.8 reproduces the bounded disassembly from that ROM (llvm-objcopy binary to elf32-littlearm, llvm-objdump armv7-none-eabi, VMA 0x80000000, file-offset ranges 0xac0..0xb50 and 0x20a8..0x22cc): the handler at 0x80000ac0 calls 0x800020a8 from 0x80000ac4, 0x80002144 from 0x80000acc and 0x800021d4 from 0x80000b10; the config helper loads 0x400 at 0x8000215c and copies 0x100 words from the +0x100 window, and the bulk helper shifts the supplied count by 10 at 0x800021e0 and clears control bit 2 at 0x800021e8.
scope: Host-only byte reading of captured X-M1 BootROM plus source inspection of sibling fffw naming and later public Milbeaut Linux drivers. This bounds software behavior and excludes only the named published register layouts, not every USB, serial, companion or board implementation. The public LLVM reproduction ran on 2026-10-26 in fresh ignored output.
limitations: The captured bytes do not identify the controller IP, electrical protocol, framing, pinmux, producer or connector.
The fffw name is sibling scope; the Linux drivers are later Milbeaut-family sources and cannot establish FF4227 identity.
Application-runtime button operation does not prove reset-time electrical state or low-selector control.
No camera, card, USB or board operation occurred.

label: hardware-observed
claim: On the failed X-M1 body, the owner used the exact reviewed startup-restored dual-path blink image after two pre-run comparisons passed. With a battery retained, Fn plus the inward sub-command-dial press held and the power switch toggled repeatedly at an estimated 0.75 second per transition without battery removal, the camera began the payload's distinctive repeating cadence: three short red intervals followed by one long red interval. The switch was subsequently left OFF and the card returned to the host. The preserved 17,826,304-byte prefix has SHA-256 4f1c632cd9ea6247899e2e97c2ed4ee5d3a1b179ea33b28908d4b974090ddbb0 and compares byte-for-byte with the prepared image. The exact cadence binds execution to the project-authored diagnostic payload. Because this occurred after the installed application became non-booting, it demonstrates an application-independent early execution foothold and satisfies R2. The identical payload is exposed through both FAT mode 1 and raw mode 2, so route, selector and exact successful switch edge remain unresolved. The same payload first showed the cadence on 2026-10-11, before the application failed: after an initial dark start the owner switched off and started again holding Fn, the sub-command-dial push and a full shutter press, and reported three roughly three-second red blinks followed by a steady red interval of probably 30 s or more, repeating for at least three groups, all illuminated intervals red, consistent with inverted LED polarity (inference). A host-reader readback after that session's further attempts matched the pinned image: the pinned image hash check passed, dd read exactly 17,826,304 bytes with snapshot SHA-256 4f1c632cd9ea6247899e2e97c2ed4ee5d3a1b179ea33b28908d4b974090ddbb0, and cmp matched the entire staged region, which excludes a retained byte difference there as the cause of the failed reproductions (E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150). After a supply cut and normal-card restoration the owner reported normal start, everything working and settings intact.
scope: Owner-reported physical X-M1 1.50 execution of the reviewed 512-byte startup-restored diagnostic payload: on 2026-10-11 on the then-healthy body and on 2026-10-12 on the failed body. The observations prove that one ROM SD path initialized, transferred and executed the payload. They do not prove mode 1, reproduce a controlled entry recipe, read internal storage or repair the installed application.

claim: A dual-route RAM-rollback recovery card produced no LED or LCD response on the failed X-M1 body on 2026-10-13. The canonical 17,826,304-byte card (emulated; image SHA-256 665baff8d4d2428f0ee768505ee5ed92bc1c97bcdd3856d7f3d1da4b5c9177ba, staging 97cc415350df01905a43f8282e7491351a0d55865040faedcc83f56bff397e4e, linked stub 8e2f4ad8e200b7f8d4c9f2c1f41c80ba453d74ace275e3fb1682985b566706e7) exposes one 262,144-byte native payload through FAT mode 1 and raw mode 2. Its guard admits only the observed ROM stack with FAT saved return 0x15c or raw saved return 0x174, emits one or two finite LED marker intervals respectively, restores its working registers, clears R0/NZCVQ and enters native reset. After installed segment 4 loads, callback 0x60c0 accepts only the stock or recorder call word at 0x71feb4, restores the recorder word to stock in RAM, performs local cache maintenance and continues original close. Captured-ROM execution through FAT reaches both kernels with the tap restored after 82,628,183 instructions; raw SD1 execution reads LBAs 0-513, stages all 262144 bytes, restores the tap and reaches both kernels after 13,875,381 instructions with no media programming. Independent review found no blocking issue, with tests covering marker ordering and counts, preserved registers, SP, R0/NZCVQ and the original-close register ABI. In the owner's attempt, through more switch repetitions than the authorized seven-transition bound and several battery removals, no finite FAT/raw route marker and no normal UI appeared. Because the attempt exceeded the bounded procedure and included multiple cold restarts, it identifies no switch edge, reset-retention state or route and is not a controlled negative for the one-operation sequence; it establishes that the earlier warm-entry recipe was not reproduced in that session.
scope: Host candidate and bounded emulation plus one owner-reported recovery attempt. It does not prove that the card image, FAT route, raw route or RAM rollback payload cannot work when entered.
sources: Owner report: repeated substantially beyond the prescribed sequence, with several battery removals, and observed no response
limitations: No passive SD-bus capture was available, so card detection, command traffic and route selection are unknown; no post-attempt card readback was reported.
The absence of the payload marker localizes failure only to before observable payload entry or to the marker output path.

The Cortex-R5F host proxy and coherent-cache substitution do not prove Cortex-R4 silicon cache behavior; the smoke shortens the 0x01000000-count marker delays and substitutes cache clean/invalidate and barrier semantics.

The raw dual carrier performs SD0 clock writes but no SD0 commands before SD1 staging; raw overlay register semantics, SD1 physical attachment and the battery-retained warm-toggle edge and minimum timing are unbound.
The repair exists only in RAM for the powered session; power-off returns to the installed image.
Canonical whole-card verification is a manually invoked pinned binary path, not a Bazel test target.

claim: The staged entry-latch recovery card staged-native-recovery-card-v6 brought the failed X-M1 1.50 body from the installed recorder-call failure into application UI in RAM, demonstrating R3 and not R4 (owner-reported hardware observation; the card's behaviour is emulated host evidence with independent byte review). Card: a canonical 17,826,304-byte X-M1 1.50 card, SHA-256 c62c4085ad4cbe402300e8171a4d52791b5fdbb6f0b8df7eba0418520daee19e, exposes a 512-byte entry-latch bootstrap through FAT mode 1 and raw mode 2. The bootstrap admits only the observed ROM stack and FAT/raw saved returns, turns the red LED steadily on before second-stage transfer, relocates itself, loads the existing 262,144-byte dual native rollback body through captured FAT reads or channel-1 raw reads, requires every FAT read's returned 16-bit byte count to equal the requested 32 KiB, invalidates instruction cache, restores registers and the saved return frame, turns the LED off and hands off with zero R0/NZCVQ. Continuous equal blinking reports guard/read refusal; the loaded body's one/two finite marker identifies FAT/raw completion. The bootstrap is SHA-256 e8bf3d9678a7e6f6787418e5d76a47d71d21414f9329b1f41aec9cbbe32aff2c and the body SHA-256 97cc415350df01905a43f8282e7491351a0d55865040faedcc83f56bff397e4e. Host evidence (emulated): Exact linked smoke passes FAT/raw success and wrong-stack, FAT-error and FAT-short-success refusals. Captured-ROM exact-card FAT execution matches the complete stage, both kernels, segment table and decoded image comparisons, restores the recorder call in RAM, completes original close and stops before primary rendezvous. An independent read-only review reconstructed bootstrap and body through both raw and FAT layouts, confirmed the exact 32 KiB count check, accepted the v16 exact FAT full path through original close, found no persistent media-write path and returned no blocking finding. Operation, under the owner's go for one attempt: destructive preparation and post-reinsertion verification of one expendable SDHC card, then one battery-retained startup holding Fn plus the inward sub-command, with at most 40 switch transitions of about 0.75 s ending ON and immediate cessation on any LED response; normal UI within 60 seconds counts as temporary recovery. Outcome: after about ten warm switch attempts the red LED became solid, then emitted a series of blinks, and the body entered application UI showing that the card was not initialized, powered from a dummy battery. The solid latch binds one-sector bootstrap admission; the subsequent marker and UI bind complete second-stage loading, installed native-loader continuation, RAM restoration of the recorder call and application startup. The repair was volatile and left persistent storage unrepaired.
scope: Owner-observed execution of staged-native-recovery-card-v6 on the failed X-M1 1.50 body, with the card's host evidence and its independent review; one attempt, no persistent repair, USB operation or post-recovery navigation.
limitations: The finite marker count was not reported, so FAT versus raw entry is unresolved.

The host fixtures are primary-only coherent-cache and ideal-device models; physical SD entry, controller timing, silicon cache visibility and display startup are observed only through this one outcome.
The source records carried no firmware hash or commands; those empty fields are missing metadata, not absence of inputs or commands.

claim: The persistent repair v2 card for the failed recorder body executed on the camera into its delayed native-stage failure loop and did not repair the body. (emulated) The canonical X-M1 1.50 card limits its requested internal-media mutation to logical block 14. Complemented media comparison between pinned RC0-prefix DAT acb0fbbb9507421f48a6254920cafb5ce20e1fd6bf821bc80c912c1f99c29ca8 and installed recorder rev-2 DAT 72a78c5595f40f88af26c4ed429529a756f759aa9b8e5c5704a745613f9ed0a8 finds only blocks 14 and 71 changed; block 14 has seven changed bytes in the compressed image-4 stream and block 71 contains the inert 846-byte recorder blob. The carried 131072-byte RC0 block 14 hashes to 94deaec641a11cf045c8761752b218d9b52af9e2e015e3b8dcc8e33708956bf5 and CRC32 0x92863e8b. The delayed post-id-6 stage restores its temporary call hook, requires storage ready, checks the source CRC and invokes exact stock writer 0x006a9268 with arguments 14, 1 and 0x00040000. Canonical card verify, FAT/raw bootstrap smoke, guard/callback/stage smoke and exact bounded-writer execution under a declared lower-device model pass. The exact v2 card is 17826304 bytes, SHA-256 92c1aaf9b22ee951aaf861caf7453bedf00112615406099835a4b3e652c8d883. Independent read-only review approved v2 with no blocking findings after v1's silent guard and callback halts were routed to repeating short-red pulses, with a behavioral smoke requiring six LED writes for each refusal case; the reviewer independently matched the RC0 and recorder inputs, the two-block difference set, the seven block-14 bytes, the block-14 SHA-256 and CRC32, raw/FAT layouts, exact branch encodings, callback and completion ABIs, cache operations, writer arguments and v2 artifact hashes, and confirmed that block 71 is not requested. The owner's go covered destructive preparation and exact readback of one expendable card, ending the current volatile recovered session, and one bounded SD-entry operation whose only requested internal-media mutation is stock writer call 0x006a9268(14,1,0x00040000), with at most 40 approximately 0.75-second power-switch transitions with Fn plus inward sub-command held. (hardware-observed, owner-reported) Card preparation readback passed, and the attempt reached ordinary application UI with the card-not-initialized message while the red LED repeated equal short pulses, the candidate's shared refusal/error path; the success indication of exactly three long pulses followed by LED-off was not observed. With the body powered and untouched the owner counted approximately 14-15 complete cycles in ten seconds and could not distinguish a second solid-red interval. The stage failure loop uses two 0x00800000 decrement delays per cycle and the bootstrap refusal loop two 0x01000000 delays, so the faster cadence with active application UI is consistent with the delayed native-stage failure loop: storage-ready mismatch, repair-source CRC mismatch or nonzero stock-writer return. Logical block 14 later read as exact RC0 (E-RECOVERY-PACKET-CODED-RC0-150), and the persistent failure was repaired by the v5 physical block-14 rollback (E-RECOVERY-RECORDER-R4-DECISION-150).
scope: Host proof of exact bytes, transfer layout, control flow and bounded stock-writer invocation, its independent source and exact-byte review, and one owner-run SD-entry attempt with passive cadence classification.
limitations: The host proof does not prove delayed code residency, silicon cache behavior, scheduler/media exclusivity, valid remap state, lower NAND verification/status semantics, atomicity, power-loss behavior or physical SD entry.

The shared short-pulse cadence does not say which of storage-ready mismatch, source-CRC mismatch or nonzero writer return occurred, or whether the writer was called; a nonzero writer result can follow a program attempt.

claim: After two conditional logical block-14 recovery runs on 2026-10-13, logical block 14 read as exact RC0 through the stock reader, yet ordinary startup stayed dark; why the stock logical reader returned RC0 while physical block 14 held recorder bytes (E-RECOVERY-PHYSICAL-PAIR-STATUS13-150) is unexplained. Both cards (emulated; independently reviewed) restore the delayed completion hook, require storage readiness and pre-read logical block 14. Exact RC0 continues without a write and an unknown CRC continues without a write; only exact recorder CRC32 0xd1943bd0 plus exact carried RC0 source CRC32 0x92863e8b reaches one stock writer call 0x006a9268(14,1,0x00040000), and every returning write is followed by a second stock read. Reader 0x006a8f1c and writer 0x006a9268 resolve logical block 14 through the same remap-table entry, and the synchronous writer releases storage serialization before returning to the post-read (source-inspected). The first card (SHA-256 361eadd6dc1ad955dc54f229a182da749706d51b6973fc9a42dc2686b6feaccc; ffboot 75f56cbf46670f3cb60ca63fa54e56a3bd0c56b7b839b6b7390c51181bef2281, ffrecov e4c15aa5ef9088787f369cc193f5d853baa850144e4b57ae9afb3b459860a18c, stage 280565af5ebddba9970e4afbe1ab5da7e2f346f428c665ac7533e653dbbf7f82) ended with application UI and a continuing red LED. In the owner's 66.4-second video VID_20261012_234225.mp4, red is continuously visible from about 25.1-27.5 seconds (the bootstrap's solid second-stage-load marker); from 28.3-30.63 seconds nine on intervals average 0.133 seconds and eight off intervals 0.142 seconds (0.275-second cycle); the cadence changes at 30.8 seconds; and 31.5-66.1 seconds holds 46 complete on and 46 complete off intervals, mean on 0.395 seconds (0.367-0.433), mean off 0.357 seconds (0.333-0.400), mean cycle 0.752 seconds (0.700-0.800), with no isolated group of one to three long pulses. That terminal cadence is the payload's repeating-slow loop, reached after an initial reader error before any write, a post-write reader error or unknown post-write data; the early short cadence cannot be the same invocation's fast loop because both loops are terminal. The pinned 1.50 bytes bind only direct red indicator writes 0xfff893c0=0x00010001/0x00010000; the body's green maintenance indicator has no X-M1 control binding, and the fffw X-E2 values at 0xfff893c0/0xfff893c4 are sibling bytes. The second, packet-coded card (SHA-256 5cf17e43929338fcfc1717d5ac7cdefe6e6d4f95670b4bd2eb43f8b087b95781; coded stage 1,144 bytes, SHA-256 135d0c7792a6e8e88e461d4c07eba17c1e75612b4a5c7039f83ae312ef036147) keeps the same gate and makes every delayed-stage outcome terminal, repeating a four-long-delay solid sync, a four-long-delay dark separator and one to nine long pulses: 1 storage-not-ready, 2 initial-read error, 3 initial unknown, 4 preexisting RC0, 5 carried-source refusal, 6 post-write read error, 7 post-write RC0, 8 post-write recorder, 9 post-write unknown; codes 1-5 precede any writer and 6-9 follow exactly one writer and the mandatory post-read. In the owner's video VID_20261013_004206.mp4 (56.8 seconds, SHA-256 fc0b9f1ca967940b4d2952684f634a77704f904bb922dae26fdf20588900705d), a fixed indicator ROI sampled at 20 Hz shows 6.00 seconds dark, 6.00 seconds lit, four 1.85-second dark notches separated by 1.85-1.90-second lit intervals and a 7.90-second lit interval, then the next packet with 5.95 seconds dark and 6.05 seconds lit. The 4:1 sync-to-pulse ratio shows the physical indicator is inverted relative to the led_on/led_off helper labels. Four notches are code 4: the initial stock read of logical block 14 had exact RC0 CRC32 0x92863e8b, and that invocation made no writer call. Two ordinary no-button startups followed with the recovery card removed and a newly host-formatted conventional MBR/FAT32 card holding no firmware: one after ending the powered session and one from supply-disconnected state. Both stayed dark, so retained dummy-power state does not explain the dark startup and logical block 14 reading RC0 through the stock reader is not sufficient for ordinary startup.
scope: Host control-flow and exact-byte proof of both conditional cards, owner videos interpreted against the reviewed packet control flow, and owner-reported ordinary startups on one X-M1 1.50 body. claim: On the recorder-failed body, both the boot-selected and the application-selected physical block for logical block 14 are physical 14, and on 2026-10-13 physical 14 held the recorder image (hardware-observed through read-only SD-booted diagnostics). Source inspection of the staged code-4 run (E-RECOVERY-PACKET-CODED-RC0-150): its early callback reaches the delayed stage only after RAM word 0x0071feb4 equals recorder call 0xeb34a9c9 and then restores that word to stock, while code 4 requires the application stock reader to return exact RC0 for logical block 14, so one boot exposed two block-14 contents. Boot record 0x00002058 scans physical blocks 0..0x139 into list 0x00004310, and 0x0000209c maps logical to physical by skipping sorted bad entries. Byte-read on the 1.50 images: the X-M1 has the gain-table stage (FUN_00d6a250, keyed 22-point records at image-4 0x825630, 226 records); at DR100 with adjustments 0 it selects record 1 for PROVIA, equal to the X70's logged PROVIA DR100 table, and record 101 (flat, unity gain) for Velvia, ASTIA and PRO Neg; its luma-band presets 1-3 (FUN_00d618a4) equal the X70's; its five chroma gains (FUN_00d60ea8) multiply to unity for all five films. With LibRaw 0.22.1 sensor matrices and 691 colorimetric patches, the PROVIA-relative fit with chroma ridged toward the PROVIA-relative 2x2 construction (output side, w 0.1) gives leave-one-out e_method (mean / p95 / max CIEDE2000 against the X-M1 stage with its real parameters) of 1.07/2.39/4.78 Velvia, 1.47/3.53/5.11 ASTIA, 1.14/2.72/4.89 PRO Neg Std and 1.28/3.83/10.38 PRO Neg Hi, against 1.18-1.90 means for the absolute fit and 1.33-3.96 for the naive baselines. Proposed thresholds for spec 19.5.6 items 1-3 are fixed in reports/classic-chrome-model.md section 7. Moving Color, Highlight, Shadow or DR (200, 400) one at a time through PROVIA's byte-read X-M1 selectors (Color gain, film chroma gain by DR, H/S gain-record family, gain record and tone key by level2) moves the candidate in the same direction as the X-Trans II Classic Chrome reference in all 14 settings (reports/classic-chrome-model.md section 6.6).

label: static-inference
claim: The X-M1 1.50 image-4 tone-record table (count word 0x824bc4, 37 records of 0x48 bytes from 0x824bc8, keys 0-36) equals the X70 1.10 section-4 records 0-36 byte for byte, keys included. The X70 table (count 42 at 0xb624e0, records from 0xb624e8) appends keys 37-41, none of which is in the X-M1 table; the X70 selects key 38 for Classic Chrome at every DR setting (x70view research/film-simulation.md). Classic Chrome's tone curve is therefore new data for the X-M1, and every stock X-M1 curve is shared with the X70. Neither of the other X-Trans CMOS I bodies' latest firmware carries Classic Chrome: X-Pro1 3.82 (SHA-256 709e26f6dd77e922660010628fb20937b269be871b188b8810eb2cb4d5d33236) and X-E1 2.71 (SHA-256 2cd3be7c65a3c269a1be230180d6da9634c37755389963705c35ae1081090a63). label: hardware-observed
claim: A stored adjustment byte 0xf7 != 0 opens the ff80 service channel in an ordinary X-M1 1.50 boot. With 0xf7 = 0x01 stored (E-STORED-F7-COMMIT-RUN-150), the owner booted XM1-body-01 (1.50 with RC0) normally without USB and then attached the cable; the host enumerated the camera as 04cb:ff80 (lsusb: Bus 005 Device 075: ID 04cb:ff80 Fuji Photo Film Co., Ltd) instead of the ordinary PTP device, and the owner reports that menus and everything else work normally while connected this way. The first ordinary-boot RAM read, session 20261016T144506Z-read-ram, completed 3 D0 0x200001 function-2 requests in one pass with no write frame after config window 0 read 0xf7 = 0x01, in 1.66 s host time: the log store at 0x400a0800 reads its header 'syslog Ver 2.3', the tick cell 0x400c0800 reads 0x00000f7c (3964 ticks, about 39.7 s of uptime at the measured 99.88 Hz), and the menu frame cell 0x009571d0 reads 16 zero bytes, consistent with no menu open. Route (static-inference over byte-read): the connect handler 0x00ecf8b8 tests f7 and *(0x009570dc), a system-mode word written once at boot by 0x00639b1c (table 0x00639c4c: application mode 3->1, 4->2, 7->5, 0xb->7), so its 'neither 5 nor 7' test excludes application modes 7 (USB-cable boot) and 0xb (maintenance) and passes ordinary power-on mode 3 (0x00635280 first calls 0x006330d8(1), pending 0->3). On attach in mode 3 it withholds the application 0x10 event, posts queue-7 0x1705 with a null callback and registers 0x00ed19e4; group-1 row 4 state 3 -> 0x00ecc2c8 -> group-0 row 0 state 0 -> 0x00ecc104 -> 0x00d82478(...,3,...) sets service mode 0x0146a0c0 = 3 and posts transport 0x3403; only in driver state 3 does 0x00d84af8 install vendor table 0x00d80cf0 (0x00d819b0) and descriptor mode 0x01469810 = 3 (other states report an error through 0x00ecfeb0 and start nothing), and GET_DESCRIPTOR 0x00d7e9e8 returns the fixed 04cb:ff80 descriptor 0x00d7ef00 instead of the template patched with PID cache[0x13e..0x13f] = 0x02b6, cache[0x104..0x105] and bcdDevice from 0x0069f520. The D0 dispatcher 0x00d80a80 and handler 0x00d803cc carry no mode test; function 2 (0x00647b1c) checks only f7 != 0 and length 1..256 and copies from any address byte by byte under the IRQ-off inter-core lock 0x007235d8. So the vendor session is not confined to mode 0xb when f7 is stored. With f7 != 0 the boot USB key record 0x0073ae10 is posted only with an UP, S1 or 0x15 record, so a button-less cable boot stays in mode 3 and the jig combination still selects mode 0xb. 0x00ec8014 (0x00ec8118) suppresses the startup application 0x10 in every mode, yet a jig session starts with 0xf7 stored and commit-f7-restore undoes it there (hardware-observed, E-STORED-F7-COMMIT-RUN-150); the ordinary updater also resets f7 to the template's 00 whenever its refresh flags *(0x014e356c + 0xc) & 3 are set (corroborated for RC0 by the 0x1e9 stamp; E-UPDATE-CONFIG-RESET-150). A cable pull in this route posts queue-7 0x1706 (0x009134f8 stays 0; its only setter runs from the jig entry's 0x9705 callback), stops the transport (0xB403 then 0xB404) and returns group-1 to state 3 via 0xB404 -> 0x00ecc380, never posting application 0x90. Every mode-3 start attempt, including one the driver refuses, fills 0x43360000..0x45a9ffff with 0xffffffff (0x00dc90f8), the firmware updater's staging buffer (other 0x00dc90f8 callers 0x00db8ad4, 0x00db8ff0, 0x00dc928c in the update path), which also holds the display module's buffer windows 0x43700000..0x44a00000 (0x006dd884). Because application mode 0xb maps to system mode 7, a stored f7 never registers the debug callback in a jig boot.
