label: hardware-observed
claim: On XM1-body-01 (1.50, RC0, healthy) with Fn plus the inward sub-command-dial press held and the reviewed blink or stage-marker cards inserted, SD-BOOT entry depends on power-switch timing. Of about 70 card-present starts that did not enter, all but two stayed dark instead of reaching the application, so the reset sample did not select mode 4: either both controls read pressed or the low selector read other than its captured 1; the two application boots are consistent with a dropped dial press. Never entered: about 25 cold starts with power removed between them, 30 switch-ons at about 3 s ON and 1 s OFF, about 9 at about 0.75 s ON and 3 s OFF, and 3 single deliberate flicks after a 10 s or longer dark start. Entered within a few switch-ons in every fast-toggle session (about 0.75 s per transition, OFF included): 2026-10-12, 2026-10-13 (about the tenth), and three sessions on 2026-10-15 (7th or 8th, about the 4th or 5th, within about 9 s). No start left to run has entered. The 2026-10-11 card-present starts, each followed by a supply cut: with the default blink card, Fn plus the inward dial press with USB disconnected stayed dark with no LED for the full 60 s; the setup-variant card gave the same no-response outcome; the startup-restored card's first start was dark; later retries with that card and battery cuts between them did not reproduce its marker, Fn plus the held dial push with or without full shutter staying dark while the owner reports other pairs booted normally with an SD-card-uninitialized warning (E-SDBOOT-CARD-ACTUATION-CONTRAST-150). One out-of-protocol start holding the record button and Fn after the first dark attempt reached the normal screen with a message described as no card initialized and blinked the red LED repeatedly, which is application-state indicator activity, not the payload. After the first attempt and the record/Fn start the owner restored the normal card and reported normal boot, settings intact and film-simulation entries retained including PRO Neg, card preparation PASS, and ordinary photo capture and playback; after the setup-variant attempt, everything present and working; after the retries, settings intact and shooting working, with playback not separately reported.
scope: Owner-run starts 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-15 on one body with two cards (7.2 GB SDHC, 59.4 GB SDXC); four 2026-10-15 sessions video-recorded and scored from frames and the owner's spoken counts.
sources: Owner reports of the 2026-10-11 attempts, the record/Fn start, the further attempts and the normal-card returns
limitations: Transition durations are owner estimates and audio counts, not instrumented switch edges.
Earlier starts are owner-reported without exact counts; the counts above are approximate.
The mechanism is unproved: a short OFF may preserve strap-source, card, controller or clock state; no other body or card model was tried.
FAT versus raw route is not identified by the cards' markers; raw mode 2 uses the WLAN SDIO channel, so entries are inferred to be FAT mode 1.

The 2026-10-11 reports are owner testimony without recording or ROM-state capture; the retries' count, pair enumeration, hold and release timing, shutter depth and durations were not supplied, and no card readback, bus trace or video binds the dark attempts to bytes or to FAT or raw selection.

Darkness does not distinguish a non-SD selection, missing payload transfer, failed handoff or a non-working indicator; the normal-boot warning does not identify a ROM selector, and the cause of the card-initialization message is not established.
Post-session returns are qualitative owner reports scoped to these events, not a recovery guarantee or hardware clearance.

label: hardware-observed
claim: Two independently reviewed stage-marker cards show that cold starts on XM1-body-01 never reach config-apply offset 0x80000510 of the mode-1 path. Both use the stock ffsys.bin plus LED writes and the startup-restored blink payload. after-apply (a53eb166...) lights the LED from the +0x348 pair table after the whole apply; before-memory-wait (a1792d56...) enables 0xfff88084 at 0x80000510 and lights the LED at 0x80000628, with only register writes and cycle-bounded delays between. Cold starts stayed dark with both (5 and 2 starts); fast toggling reached the blink payload with both, the before-memory-wait card at 109.6 s of video_2026-10-15_22-35-10 with 3.4 s lit and 3.2 s dark steps. Static-inference over the byte-read ROM: either the reset-time sample selected another handler (the low selector 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 reading other than its captured 1; a race between boot-ROM paths), or mode 1 ran and stopped in mount attempts 0x80000830 (each re-running channel bring-up 0x80001308 with the card-supply restart at 0x8000155c, the 12,582,912-cycle wait at 0x800015c8 and the 48,076,923-cycle card start-up limit at 0x800012dc), the FAT/ffsys.bin read, or the apply waits at 0x80000354, 0x80000b50 and 0x80000448.
scope: Host-built, reviewed card bytes; owner-run starts on 2026-10-15; static-inference over the pinned ROM (SHA-1 bed698ed1d91b5c29ce7c5d650156e6100c32cce).
commands: devenv shell -- bazel run //host/firmware:build-boot-card -- verify-stage-marker after-apply PINNED_DAT PAYLOAD_BIN private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/stage-marker-blink-card/diagnostic-sd.img

limitations: The physical LED effect of 0xfff88084 and the 0xfff893c4 setup is inferred from earlier lit sequences, so a marker that ran unseen cannot be fully excluded; the warm runs show the markers do not block the payload.

A lit marker during a warm success lasts too briefly to see, because the payload's first write turns the LED off.

A passive SD command, response and data capture could separate payload-sector transfer from pre-load failure without new card bytes, but not DMA delivery or execution (static-inference), and a missing signal on an unqualified or partial capture is not negative evidence. On 2026-10-11 the owner had no analyzer or breakout and declined to acquire one; a sniffer test-fitted on 2026-10-20 bent the slot contacts (E-SD-SLOT-DAMAGE-150).

label: hardware-observed
claim: Test-fitting an SD-bus sniffer whose card blade lacked the push-push latch recess bent XM1-body-01's SD slot contacts at positions 2 (DAT3), 3 (CMD) and 4 (GND), counted from the chamfered corner, and damaged the latch. NO MEMORY CARD shows with the slot empty; CARD ERROR showed with a card detected (boot-time GPIO 0xfff89314 reads 0x28, card-detect bit 7 asserted). After the contacts were re-formed, an empty adapter inked with dry-erase marker was scraped at all nine positions; diode-mode readings against the frame were 0.472 to 0.484 V on the six signal lines, 0.539 V on VDD and 0 on both grounds; 5-6 and 8-9 showed no continuity, and contacts 1 to 3 drop into separate cavities when pressed. A card inserted over a plastic shim and held home by the closed door worked for capture and playback across 7 power cycles. Shutdowns at full card insertion coincided with the card edge folding contact 2 down (owner judgement).
scope: XM1-body-01 slot after the 2026-10-20 sniffer fit; owner inspection, meter readings and power cycles.

limitations: The latch no longer holds a card: insertion needs the shim and the closed door keeps the card seated, so each card swap risks folding contact 2 again.

The camera's card supply was not measured; the shutdowns' cause is inferred.

label: static-inference
claim: On X-M1 1.50 a USB attach selects ff80 or PTP only through connect handler A 0x00ecf8b8: on a latch change it reads cache[0xf7] through 0x0069f8fc at 0x00ecf900 and, with a nonzero byte and system mode word 0x009570dc neither 5 nor 7, takes the attach arm (queue-7 0x1705, service mode 3, descriptor 04cb:ff80), otherwise the application arm (event 0x10/0x90). All 13 0xf7 reads go through the RAM cache pointer 0x0096ca50, and the setter 0x0069fc94 stores there with no other effect, so flipping the RAM byte at the attach edge changes the personality for the rest of the boot without a storage write. The USB toggle replaces the bl at 0x00ecf900 (ebdf3ffd -> ebf492d3) with a 22-word stub at 0x00bf4454 that, on an attach edge with KEY_Q's debounced driver state 0x006a0d00(0x32) set (condition row 19 at 0x00828334, byte +0x15, written only by key-driver code in 0x006a0cc4-0x006a3084; Q is debounced by 0x006a2fa8, chosen by the scan loop 0x006a3478-0x006a34a4 because the row lacks flag +0x04 & 0x100) and mode not 5 or 7, flips cache[0xf7] through 0x0069fc94. The extent [0x00bf4454, 0x00bf44e4) is referenced by no branch, aligned or unaligned word, movw/movt pair, ADR or Thumb branch in images 4, 5, plain and 2, both loaders and both boot records. Q (0x32) has no 0x00632950 or 0x006a0d00 key-state test and no role in any stock power-on or attach combination. usbcont (task 7) has a 0xc00-byte stack (creation block 0x00ed1120); the stub adds 28 bytes below its entry, fewer than handler A's stock callees reach. The updater completion 0x00db91e0 reloads the template and commits the whole area when flag word 0x014e3578 has bit 0 or 1, which header parser 0x00db9cd4 sets from the restore-list descriptors at DAT offsets 0x244-0x25b; the stock, CC and both toggle DATs carry both descriptors, so an install stores 0xf7 = 0.
scope: Pinned X-M1 1.50 decodes (id4, id5, plain, id2, both loaders, both boot records) and the stock, CC and toggle DAT headers; host-only static analysis. No camera or USB device was touched.

The stack bound is the direct-call depth plus the emulated high-water mark; indirect calls are not bounded statically.
The power-on key variant was not built; the content of the boot key records at 0x0073ae10 for a held Q is unproved.

label: static-inference
claim: The X-M1 1.50 kernel IRQ registration routines clear a source's whole 32-source enable group and restore it afterwards, on the calling core's own controller bank. In kernel0 (base 0x40000), FUN_00042b00 reads the group's enable word (0x42bb8 e51eefff), writes 0xffffffff to clear register 0xfffb30a0+4*group (0x42bc8 e3e06000 mvn r6,#0; 0x42bcc e50e6fff str), and writes saved|bit to set register 0xfffb3080+4*group at 0x42d64 (e782c103). FUN_00042eb0 does the same with an all-ones clear at 0x42f48 (e502cfff, value from 0x42f44 e3e0c000) and restores saved&~bit at 0x42fe0 (e7832105). Bank 0xfffb3000 or 0xfffb4000 is chosen by FUN_000427b8 (0x427b8 ee121e10 mrc p14 c2, compared with 0x4003). The window is guarded only by the local CPSR.I set in FUN_00042574 (0x42574 e3a00080, 0x4259c e10f1000). kernel1 (base 0xd0000) contains the same clear sequences at 0xd2bc8 and 0xd2f44. In the retained emulator, quantum boundaries can fall inside this window, and scheduled device callbacks, device ticks and the other core's quantum then observe the group as disabled. The retained emulator's interrupt controller latches a source raised inside the window and delivers it when the group is restored (emulated): a line that a clear-enable write disables stays owned by its bank until the next set-enable write to its group on that bank; a raise at an owned, masked line sets pending, and that write delivers it if it re-enables the line and discards only the window-latched request otherwise. The rule lives in Rust (emulation/xm1-upstream/native/src/irq_mask.rs); the inherited Python controller keeps the bank words and register dispatch and calls it for enable writes, raises and routing. Image data routes (image_stream and the image-work data profile), producer_stream, display_timing, the application timer and both control-bus profiles route through these owners instead of live enable bits, so an event inside the window is no longer dropped or refused. A source with no owner, or with two where it needs exactly one, still refuses. Ten Rust tests cover one case per listed source (raise inside a 0x42b00-style clear-all/restore window, not deliverable inside, deliverable after) plus unregistering restore, pre-window pending, other-bank and refusal cases. On the stock-DAT flash-boot-check and the cardless volatile RAM-push e2e the change is not observable: the flash-boot receipt equals emuverify-3 in every milestone instruction count, menu and frame hash (SHOOTING MENU 1/5/2), and all 7 e2e observation files are byte-identical to the EmuVerify-merge run, allocation 0x00a81be0.
scope: Host-only static analysis of the official X-M1 1.50 kernel images and source inspection of emulation/xm1-upstream/emulator, 2026-10-23, and the retained emulator's latch rule with its Rust tests and two acceptance runs on one workstation, 2026-10-24 (agent/IrqLatch on 9d28ba1). Upstream lead: x70view 27141c63b0 (owner commit) and 8629456bd1 (jitl), both reported against X70/XQ2; X-M1 facts come from our bytes only. No camera or USB device was touched.

label: static-inference

Byte-read in image 5: D0 dispatcher 0x00d80a80 sends 0x450006 (compare 0x00d80bb8) to case 0x00d80c54 -> 0x00d806c8, which reads the LE32 tag at request +0x10 (0x00d7f40c) and calls 0x00d8270c(tag, 0x01469878, 0x0146987c); that forwards to slot +0xc of the table at *(0x0146a0c4), 0x00dc7874 in the 0x00dc7460 template (declared at 0x00dc746c). Its tag-0x80 arm (0x00dc78bc cmp r0,#0x80 -> 0x00dc79c0) calls 0x00dbd09c, which stores pointer 0x4b2ece00 and capacity 0x100000, adding 0x8000 when 0x006fbaa4 (word 0x008fc864) returns 1; 0x00d806c8 then writes the capacity at reply +0x14 through 0x00d7f384 and the available length is 32. Transport dispatcher 0x00d7fae8 clears 0x01469c9c on every command and routes 0xe1 to 0x00d7fa4c, which reads BE32 offset at +2, BE32 length at +6 and BE16 SID at +10, refuses an inactive session (0x01469898), a SID mismatch (0x0146989a) and length 0, then sets 0x01469c9c=1, length 0x01469868 and offset 0x01469880 with no bound. 0x00d7efd4 (slot +0x14 of ff80 table 0x00d7f314) on that flag returns length min([0x01469868],[0x0146987c]) and source [0x01469878]+[0x01469880] (0x00d7f01c-0x00d7f044), a 32-bit sum; its other branch is the D1 source of E-DBG-C0-FIELD-150. None of these routines reads cache byte 0xf7. Only the 0x450006, 0x550001 (0x00d80844) and 0x580000 (0x00d80924) handlers rewrite 0x01469878/0x0146987c, so one tag-0x80 query serves repeated E1 reads. The path is bound end to end from bytes. Query: D0 accepts 32 to 512 request bytes (0x00d7f80c); 0x00d806c8 reads only the opcode and the LE32 tag at +0x10, and its 32-byte reply holds the opcode echo, error words at +4/+8 and the LE32 capacity at +0x14 with every other byte zero; (0,0) with capacity 0x100000 or 0x108000 is tag 0x80, (1,0xffff) a null slot +0xc or unknown tag (the earlier published pair stays), (9,1) a request under 32 bytes; D1 is one-shot. Callback table: only 0x00d82494 in 0x00d82478 stores 0x0146a0c4, and only its mode-3 caller 0x00ecc104 -> 0x00ecfa60 -> 0x00dc74b4 installs a table with nonzero slots, copying template 0x00dc7460 to 0x015c22a0 so slot +0xc is 0x00dc7874 (the ordinary-boot pointer 0x015c22a0 and slot 0x00dc7874 are hardware-observed in the ram-alloc records); the mode-2 and mode-4 tables 0x00ed0444 and 0x00ed0488 have zero slots +0..+0xc. Consumer: USB event handler 0x00d7d154 calls class-table slot +0x14 (0x00d7efd4, table 0x00d7f314 registered at 0x01469774 when 0x0146a0c0 = 3) and passes its pointer and length to 0x00d7c92c, which programs one DMA descriptor through 0x00d7c858: source & ~0xC0000003 to 0xfff55824, length rounded up to 64 and masked to 0x0ffffffc to 0xfff55828, the exact byte count to 0xfff55124; no CPU copy or bounce buffer exists, and 0x00d7bfc4 cleans and invalidates the whole local D-cache by set/way (loader 0x00042634(0,0)) before each DMA. D1 replies take the same path. Wrap: 0x00d7f01c-0x00d7f044 is a plain 32-bit add of base and offset with an unsigned min of length and capacity, and nothing downstream compares source or end, so the DMA reaches ((0x4b2ece00 + offset) mod 2^32) & 0x3ffffffc inside [0,0x40000000) physical, both address aliases name one physical byte, and ROM and 0xfff MMIO are unreachable. Side effects: E1 sets 0x01469c9c, 0x01469868 and 0x01469880, which completion does not clear; 0x00dbd09c only stores the pointer and capacity and reads 0x008fc864 (no storage open, MMIO or pool reservation); each DMA completion posts transport event 0x340e to queue 0x24 and sends a 2-byte interrupt-IN status, and a rejected E1 sends its code on interrupt IN after which the bulk-IN source returns no data. MPU (boot-40048 0x19e4-0x1a58): region 0 [0,0x40000000) RACR 0x303 write-back, region 1 [0x40000000,0x80000000) RACR 0x30c non-cacheable shareable, region 2 [0x80000000,2^32) device; these are windows, not a DRAM size. label: reported
claim: tiredboffin's fffw wiki page 'Note on unbricking EXR cameras' (wiki commit 7b387068f869847055c2ca1b075f8603369c05a9, 2026-10-22) states, for EXR, EXR Pro and EXR II bodies: the boot ROM can load stage 0 from a FAT card holding ffsys.bin (hardware configuration) and ffboot.bin (stage 0) when the SD-boot keys, typically Fn plus the back dial, are held at power-on; the ROM writes 1 to 0xfff88084 early (listing 0x800000e4-0x800000ec), writes 0 on failure paths after which the system powers off about 10,000 CPU cycles later, and on the normal path writes ffsys +0x10 bit 0 there; NAND ffsys has the bit clear, so the body powers off unless later code writes 1 in time; SD loading, especially of a stage 0 larger than one sector, can lose power first; the remedy is to set bit 0 of the byte at ffsys +0x10 on the SD recovery image. It also reports two recovery shapes, reusing the firmware's NAND programming function to rewrite one block (one successful experiment) and a loader built from a patched standard DAT that runs the stock updater.
scope: Sibling-family report covering EXR, EXR Pro and EXR II; it names no body or firmware version. A lead for SD-BOOT-CARD-ENTRY-01 and recovery-status; X-M1 bindings are recorded separately in E-SDBOOT-NOTE-HOLD-BINDING-150.

git -C /tmp/fffw.wiki grep -i -e licen -e copyright (no match in the note; the wiki carries no terms of its own)
limitations: The page carries no license or terms; the fffw repository's MIT grant covers repository source, not the wiki. The note is cited and paraphrased, not copied.
The ten-thousand-cycle power-off latency, the power-hold meaning of the bit and the NAND-path re-hold are stated without a capture or a named body.

label: static-inference
claim: On X-M1 1.50 the ROM sets 0xfff88084 bit 0 at init, the config apply replaces it with ffsys.bin +0x10 bit 0, which every held card clears, and no later code of an ordinary boot sets it again, yet the body runs; each code point of the fffw unbricking note (E-FFFW-UNBRICK-NOTE-REPORTED) binds to the captured ROM, and its NAND-path premise does not (static-inference over byte reads). Byte-read: 0x800000e4-0x800000ec hold e59f013c, e3a01001, e5801084 with literal 0x80000228 = 0xfff88000, identical to the note's listing; the apply 0x80000304 loads r1=0xfff00004 (literal 0x80000a88), then 0x80000328 ldr r2,[r1,#0x10], 0x8000032c and r2,r2,#1, 0x80000330 str r2,[r6,#0x84] with r6=0xfff88000. The apply is called by modes 1 (0x800008a0), 2 (0x800007a0), 3-6 (0x80000a20) and 7 (0x80000aec) and returns 0 on every decoded path, so its faults are hangs after 0x80000330. Apart from configuration-driven pair and optional-slot writes (used by the stage markers), the ROM's other stores to 0xfff88084 are the failure writes at 0x800002fc, 0x8000085c, 0x80000754, 0x80000980 and 0x80000ae0 and the teardown 0x80000b48 (callers 0x80000800, 0x8000091c, 0x80000a5c and 0x80000b20), whose argument is +0x10 bit 1 on ffboot read failure (0x80000e4c stores through the 0xfff52800 media base); +0x10 is read only for bit 0 (0x80000328), bit 1 and bits 10:8 (modes 1, 2 and 3-6) and bit 1 (mode 7, 0x80000b04). No delay follows any failure store: handlers return -1 and the dispatch reaches wfi at 0x80000020, so the note's 10,000-cycle latency is not ROM code. ROM strings ffsys.bin and ffboot.bin sit at +0xa9c and +0xaa8. All 57 ffsys.bin/FFSYS.BIN files under private-data/ (42 under analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/) hold +0x10 = 0x300 (55 files) or 0x302 (stage-marker and memory-marker cards), bit 0 clear, as does the update payload's own config block. A literal and movw/movt scan finds no store of 1 to 0xfff88084 in the 256 KiB native staging span, boot-40048/boot-50048, loader-40000/loader-d0000 or image 5, and the boot records and kernels contain no literal or movw/movt reference to 0xfff88000-0xfff880ff; image 4's only writer, 0x00656a08-0x00656a20 at the end of GPIO-bank initialization 0x006568ec, clears bit 0. The upstream X-E2 startup writes 0xfff88084=1 before its blink code; of the project payloads only the startup-restored blink variant and later 512-byte payloads write 1 themselves, after the ROM's whole ffboot.bin read (E-SDBOOT-BLINK-STARTUP-CANDIDATE-150). A stock internal-media boot therefore runs with the bit released from 0x80000330 and still boots, so on X-M1 a release while the switch is ON is not by itself a power-off.
scope: Host byte reads of the captured X-M1 ROM, the DAT-derived native staging span, boot records, kernels and images 4 and 5, and every ffsys file held, plus ordinary-boot behaviour already observed on XM1-body-01. The power-hold meaning of bit 0, the X70/X100S release timings and the fffw wiki's power-off claim are sibling reports only.
commands: grep of private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/bootrom.dis for 'str* rN, [rM, #0x84]', literal 0xfff88000 and its pool loads (0xa70, 0x228)
read +0x10 of every ffsys.bin/FFSYS.BIN under private-data/
literal (0xfff88000, 0xfff88084) and movw/movt scans over the complemented DAT [0x4025c,0x8025c), decode/boot-40048.bin, boot-50048.bin, loader-40000.bin, loader-d0000.bin, id4 and id5
limitations: The scans find literal and movw/movt address constructions; a computed address, Thumb code in the boot records or an MCU-side hold would escape them.
Unproven: what bit 0 controls on X-M1, whether this body cuts supply while bit 0 is clear during a slow card read, and the release limit (E-SDBOOT-NOTE-FLICK-TEST-150).
The installed internal-media configuration block is assumed equal to the update payload's (+0x10 = 0x300).
The note's key combination binds only as far as E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150: Fn plus the inward rear sub-command-dial press, entering only under fast power toggling.

label: static-inference
claim: The hypothesis that the fffw unbricking note explains the on-off flick (SD-BOOT entry on XM1-body-01 only under 0.75-second power toggling) is open. Against it: the release at 0x80000330 happens identically on every start, so it does not predict the timing dependence of E-SDBOOT-ENTRY-TIMING-150; cold starts stop before 0x80000510 although toggled starts survive the far longer post-release interval to the payload's own store of 1; ordinary boots release the bit and run (E-SDBOOT-NOTE-HOLD-BINDING-150). For a size effect: every card that entered had a 512-byte ROM-read ffboot.bin that stores 0xfff88084 = 1 before any long load (startup-restored blink 30b8f5c0..., both stage markers, staged bootstraps e8bf3d96..., 75f56cbf..., 4694c27d..., 7f3a3db4... at byte 0x1b4; the later three differ from v6 only in four to six sector-count immediate bytes), while the only toggled session that never entered used the dual-native card, whose 262,144-byte ROM-read stage first stores 1 in its 0x6000 guard after the whole read (E-DUAL-NATIVE-RECOVERY-NO-ENTRY-150); the staged v6 card, which writes 1 and then loads the same 256 KiB itself, entered about two hours later (E-STAGED-RECOVERY-SUCCESS-150). A supply that stays on while the switch is ON or bit 0 is set fits every observation and explains why toggled entry needs an early hold, not why entry needs toggling. A cold start of a card with ffsys +0x10 bit 0 set decides the hypothesis.
scope: Comparison of the note's mechanism with existing hardware-observed records of XM1-body-01 and the byte content of the cards used; no new camera observation.
commands: ls -l and sha256sum of ffboot.bin/ffrecov.bin in every card directory under private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/
xxd -p -c4 FFBOOT | grep -n '^84[0-9a-f]008e3$' (movw rN,#0x8084) for the staged bootstraps, the blink payload and the dual-native stage
limitations: The dual-native no-entry is one uncontrolled session with more transitions than authorized and battery removals; it is not a controlled negative.
Switch state at each marker onset was never recorded, so whether bit 0 holds supply against the switch is unobserved.
Transition times are owner estimates and audio counts.

label: static-inference
claim: X-M1 1.50 MPU region programming is mapped from byte-read register writes. The boot ROM programs regions 0-4 at 0x80000040-0x800000cc: region 0 base 0 size 63 access 0x1304 (XN set), region 1 base 0 size 59 access 0x30c, region 2 base 0x40000000 size 59 access 0x130c, region 3 base 0x80000000 size 27 access 0x308, region 4 base 0xfff00000 size 23 access 0x30c. Boot record boot-40048 then reprograms them: helper 0x1a84 writes RGNR (c6,c2,0) = r1, DRACR (c6,c1,4) = r2, DRBAR (c6,c1,0) = r3 << 16 and DRSR (c6,c1,2) = r4 | 1, and the caller at 0x19e4-0x1a58 visits five regions: region 0 (0x19e8-0x19f8) base 0, access 0x303 (literal 0x1adc), size field 58 so 1 GiB, giving [0,0x40000000) normal write-back no write-allocate, non-shared, XN clear; region 1 base 0x40000000, access 0x30c, 1 GiB, normal non-cacheable shareable; region 2 base 0x80000000, access 0x305 (literal 0x1ae0), size field 60 so 2 GiB, shareable device; region 3 base 0xfff00000, access 0x30c, size field 22 so 4 KiB; region 4 base 0xffff0000, access 0x303, size field 30 so 64 KiB, programmed only when r0 is nonzero (0x1a3c). 0x1a5c-0x1a7c then sets SCTLR bits 0x1005 (M, C, I) after a DSB, the c15,c5,0 write and ICIALLU, so the boot ROM's XN region 0 is not the final state. Image 4 sets only regions 5-7 (setter 0x61c700, helper 0x73ba50, heap bases via 0x7235d8). The RC0 window at 0x0061c1fc and image 4's executing code share region 0, 1 GiB with XN clear, and no subregion is disabled (DRSR bits 15:8 are zero), so the window carries the same execute permission; this removes the prefix-executability residual of E-FILE-CARRY-DESIGN-150. E-BULK-READ-PATH-150 and reports/af-observe-instruments-150.md section 9.7 read the same boot-record map.
scope: Pinned X-M1 1.50 boot ROM block, decoded boot record boot-40048 and decoded images, host-only static reading; no MPU behavior is observed.
commands: nix shell nixpkgs#llvm -c llvm-objcopy -I binary -O elf32-littlearm --rename-section=.data=.text,code,alloc,load,readonly,contents private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/decode/boot-40048.bin boot.elf
limitations: Register programming is byte-read; MPU behaviour on the inferred R4F-class core is unobserved and no R5 TCM or cache semantics are assumed.
Execute permission is inferred from the shared region and subregion, not from an executed instruction at 0x0061c1fc.
Which core takes the region-4 branch rests on the caller setting r0 from 0x1aa0, which compares the CP14 c2 identity with 0x4003; the caller is outside the listed range.
The boot ROM region list and the image-4 regions 5-7 come from the earlier reading in reports/af-observe-instruments-150.md section 9.7 and were not re-read with the boot record.
Later region writes by code outside the mapped setters are not excluded.

claim: The complete builder emits a format-2 source package with a 32-byte header and exactly 0xa120 CRC-32/ISO-HDLC-covered image bytes, including validator, publication table, copy/store passes, kernel and names. The linked trusted gate occupies 48+48+96+96=288 bytes and reads the source without a payload RAM store until CRC matches and the whole source table validates. Its checked-source validator is 120 bytes, bounded to 128 slots with a required zero/zero terminator, and uses immutable aligned nonwrapping windows [0x0061c400,0x0089ec00), [0x00bf1a00,0x010c1a20) and [0x01100000,0x01180000). Only then does the 32-byte copy pass populate the runtime carve and the 60-byte store/cache pass publish. Independent emitted-byte review accepts that component under the explicit stable-source/instruction-fetch premise. A fresh complete DAT passes builder round trips and carried-part checks, a separate final-DAT verification passes 45 contract checks, and its extracted plain bytes match the entire source package. All seven extracted boot sections match their final image/package spans. The guarded native run passes all 30 boot cases with no memory or register mismatches: valid publication and all six legal window endpoints; exact-length, old-format, truncated/high-water and loader-wait refusals; CRC refusal including the old rotate-add-preserving collision; and repaired-CRC unterminated, malformed-terminator and late-invalid-destination tables. Every refusal compares the entire runtime carve, with status 2 as the sole permitted change, and every publication output against its initial bytes. Success compares the copied image, untouched tail/status and publication words, then stops at the first DSB. The run executes 14 to 1426927 instructions per case and completes through the canonical one-slot thermal guard in 52.860 seconds, peaking at 6.2 GiB with zero swap; Tctl reads 51.250 C before admission and after completion. Host package-refusal, recipe-bank/CRC and RAM-layout suites pass. The format-1 stub occupied the four census-proven runs (entry 48 bytes at 0x78319c, check 96 at 0x78d4f8, sum 48 at 0x782348, publish 96 at 0x789e2c), the same 288-byte budget the format-2 gate fills. A larger ten-run home is void: six of its runs hold the live FILM 1-3 bracket pointer pairs (0x786794/0x786798, 0x786dc8/0x786dcc, 0x7898f4/0x7898f8), which this candidate line does not retarget (byte-read; E-RECIPE-D3-PATCH-150). Cell 0x00914834 holds a stage-relative bytes-copied count, not an address: helper 0x73b924 is formed only at 0x6a98a4 in the stage-6 plain loader (static driver-path read), so the loader-wait predicate is cell >= RB_SRC_END - 0x01100000 with boot.stage_base = 0x01100000. Requirements established on the format-1 stub by review and by its 17 bounded boot-copy cases (2026-10-10), which bind any boot gate: the stock return LR is 0x0069d2e4; a length gate precedes any store, since a zero or unaligned image_bytes wraps the copy counter into a write storm over the address space; the copied destination gets a D-cache clean and I-cache invalidate before any fetch; the image bound must not reach the status cell at 0x00befffc; the contract's MOVT replacement goes e3403037 to e34030be; nothing is published before the sum over the summed image matches, and every publication address comes from summed bytes; the cache-maintenance calls go through the link-relocated symbols rb_cache_dclean_inval (0x0061c4f4) and rb_cache_iinval (0x0061c4ec) defined in the .ld, because numeric bl operands assembled by llvm-mc became raw imm24 offsets to 0x00da634c/0x00da6350 and skipped the maintenance. Success leaves the status cell unchanged and only refusal writes 2, so a stale 2 from an earlier boot misreads on a warm boot; diagnostics corroborate against the bank's presence. The format-1 stub's accepted-in-principle review is withdrawn for its publication properties (E-FLASH-READINESS-AUDIT-150): it did not enforce checksum coverage of its table, bounded table termination or destination bounds, which format 2's checked-source validator enforces.

label: emulated

Registers r4-r11, sp, exit pc, the guarded destination, the slot tables and the caller frame match; owned stack use is at most 96 bytes against stock 84. Five refusal controls and one acceptance control are judged as required. A static scan of loaders A and B, image 2, stock and package images 4 and 5 and plain image 6 finds 3,027 direct BL sites into the eleven entries and no data, formed or interior reference. The bank's SELECT refresh calls the owned store; the bank allowlist passes without 0x0061ceac. With the native suites' default bank base moved to 0x00be0000, the default UI command passes 55/55 with its controls rejected; at the former 0x00be1f00 the bank ends at 0x00bebbb4, past the plan name record 0x00beb784, and 51 cases stop as memory_guard.
scope: Legacy native runner, one call per case with fixed read-only frame, values and navigation inputs, and the default 55-case UI suite. No packaged or device-driven route and no publication over the stock entries. 0x00be0000 is a native-case placement, not a hardware placement.

claim: On FujiMod's EXR II runtime built from staging fed7cfc, stock X-M1 1.50 with f7-1.nand cold-boots on a private copy of a 4 GiB FAT32 superfloppy holding one owner X-M1 JPEG in DCIM/963_FUJI. One PLAY input (GPIO2.9 low, key row 12) is consumed by the render settle. UI mode 0x009500ec goes from 3 to 4 with previous mode 3: 0x00d350c4 is entered with r0=2 and the 3-to-4 setup 0x00d1ba2c runs. Media status 0x00918af8 stays 1 with no cached warning. The file client reads the JPEG twice, 0x19000 bytes into 0x45fc9c00 and then 0x341338 bytes directly after them, the whole 3,515,192-byte file. Every CMD18 still in the 32-entry SD history overlaps the file's sectors, the last ending at its final data sector. EXIF parser 0x011c36f8 runs. The 0xfff63000 start 0x0065a548 and its IRQ-0x4c handler 0x00d99570 each run once after each file read; FujiMod's jpeg-decoder raises that interrupt only after a completed decode DMA. The final 720x480 frame shows the photograph under the playback overlay 963-3095, 1/100, F4.5, ISO 6400, 2026.10. 9 11:01 AM, which matches the file's EXIF; reviewer inspection of the PNG confirms a playback photograph. No SD write is accepted and the file reads back unchanged through media-read.
scope: One emulated cold-boot PLAY route on the stock DAT with one card fixture; ordinary single-frame playback entry and its first displayed image, not capture, save, browsing, deletion or RAW conversion.
limitations: 0x00d0ad8c is not entered, so the live-view PLAY path reaches 0x00d350c4(2) through an unidentified caller.

The playback decode requester is bound only statically: 0x01220294 calls 0x00d9882c(0x014eae2c) -> 0x00d99714, whose 0x0065a58c programs decoder input +0x10c, length +0x110 and output +0x100 from job words +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20; the observed file-I/O return addresses lie in the same module (0x01220314, 0x01220378, 0x012203a4). The run neither traced that requester nor read the programmed words, so the file offset, length, output and downscale of each decode are unobserved.
The first 28 completed SD commands of the route fell outside the 32-entry history.
Decoded pixels are not compared with a reference decode; display colour, scaling and timing fidelity are unproved.
The frames before the press show the PROGRAM AE dial guide after the mode-dial hold, not live view.

claim: On FujiMod's EXR II runtime built from staging fed7cfc, stock X-M1 1.50 runs with the JPEG card in P mode and SHOOT WITHOUT LENS ON set through stock menu keys. It admits one S2 contact (GPIO0.3, key row 6) with no host S1. The firmware's own S1 record reaches 0x00c58c38, and the 0x00d24e34 result at 0x00c58ccc is 0. Command 2 takes recorder machine 0x15 through 0x00e1c758, which submits operation 0x39 and leaves state 5. Properties 0x1b1 (u32[0x00956844]) and 0x13a (u32[0x00956974]) read 0. Modal 0x4a action 29 0x00c595f4 then posts mailbox 0x71, and 0x00d1350c issues request 0x206. Machine 0x4e receives 0x206 and issues command 0x1a. Its state-6 action 0x00e360ec then runs for each of 0x134f, 0x139e, 0x13a0, 0x139f, 0x13c6, 0x13a1, 0x13c6 and 0x13a2, and each run issues command 0x19 to machine 0x15. Machine 0x15 stays in state 5, and its idle handler 0x00e1d3cc never runs. Machine 0x4e reaches state 9. Its only later message, 0x1351, reaches 0x00e36208, where 0x00dd6820(0x19) returns 0. That query goes to machine 0x4d row 10 in state 1 (0x00e34ed4), which returns the result of 0x00ddb5cc. 0x00ddb5cc returns 1 only when both machine 0x14's query row and machine 0x12's message-class row return 1, combined through table 0x00de28fc. UI notification 0x837 reaches 0x00d27c7c, and 0x00c6c938 sets modal 0x4a to state 8. 0x00c6ce48 then returns 1, 1, 1, 4, 1 and 1. u32[0x0095154c] reads 0xe, so a 0x816 completion would restore state 4, but neither the 0x816 publisher 0x00e1eaf4 nor modal 0x1f's 0x816 action 0x00c30c54 runs. Later, 0x00edb630 calls 0x00d9f0b0(u32[0x016994f8], 0x80, 0x01698a74, 0). At 0x00d9f348 that call opens image-input channel 2 through 0x00663040 with callback 0x00ed84cc. The firmware channel table at 0x009431f8 then holds channel 2 open with that callback, registered for line 36 with handler 0x00664c28. 0x00edb630 sets stream mode u32[0x01698a54]=1. In that mode, 0x00ed84cc re-arms channel 2 and calls the client pointer u32[0x01698a58]. The bound candidate clients, 0x00fe9624 and 0x00ffa588, post message 0x3f08 to queue 0x2f. For at least 117,979,205 summed instructions after the open, at least 4,915,800 ticks at 24 instructions per tick, none of the line-36, line-37 or line-38 handlers runs. No codec, encoder, save-chain, file or SD write runs. The last two 40,000,000-instruction windows enter no traced or fixed site. FujiMod's image-input model starts the channel-2 DMA only in frame(), which requires options.sensor_period_ticks and wiring.sensor, and this run document declares both null. The final display capture finds no configured plane. No strict model stop occurs.
scope: Emulated S2-contact routes on the stock DAT with one card fixture: one 40M-window run and one traced three-window probe. This records the state observed after the contact and its bound recorder, UI and image-input chain. It is not capture, save or shutter behavior, and not a sole cause.
limitations: One S2 contact with no host S1; not a mechanical half-then-full shutter sequence. SHOOT WITHOUT LENS ON with no lens model differs from the owner's body.
Whether channel 2 carries the still exposure or an AF or statistics stream is not bound. Neither the queue-0x2f consumer of 0x3f08 nor the 0x00edb630 caller that ran is bound.

A missing channel-2 frame is an observed prerequisite, not a demonstrated sole cause. The recorder message that would complete machine 0x4e state 9 is unbound, as are the 0x816 producer and any further lens, sensor-serial, shutter-comparator, timer or CPU1 wait.
0x0066382c, 0x0065e2c4 and 0x0065f8bc write the channel-2 format, destination, stride and width from 0x01698a74, but the values were not observed, and the writer of the height register is unbound.
The tick count is a lower bound; the bridge does not export FujiMod idle-skip time.
The UI notification poster 0x00dcb6c0 was not traced in these runs; E-FUJIMOD-XM1-S2-RAW-WINDOW-150 observes it posting 0x816 in live view before a press.

label: source-inspected
claim: X-M1 1.50 source distinguishes physical S1 GPIO0.2/IRQ10 from S2 GPIO0.3/IRQ11. Handler 0x006a2e00 toggles cached contact state; publisher 0x006a1c50 prepends input 7 on input 8 when cached input 7 is released, then marks that cache pressed. An S1 action without an S1 IRQ therefore does not establish held physical S1. Recorder predicate machine 0x14 is selected by 0x00dfa674, with row/state cells 0x015457b8/0x01545878, width 19, matrix 0x00e3f638 and action table 0x00e3bf28. Command 0x19 with message 0x1351 selects row 12. At observed state 2, cell 0x00e3f804 contains action 25 and transition 1; action 0x00e152e8 posts UI 0x839 and returns 0, while transition pointer 1 is null. Predicate machine 0x12 is selected by 0x00ddb3ac -> 0x00dfa144, with row/state cells 0x015457b4/0x01545874, width 13, matrix 0x00e3fc28 and action table 0x00e3c10c. Class 10 with message 0x1351 selects default row 25; at state 0, cell 0x00e3feb2 contains action 2=0x00e0d604, whose A32 body returns constant 1, and null transition 1. Combiner 0x00dd68b8 maps inputs (0,1) to byte 6 of 0x00de28fc, which is 0. The observed blocking side is thus machine 0x14, not machine 0x12. Machine 0x14's 0x206 action 0x00e1357c enters state 2 and calls 0x00dd6e98 -> 0x00e668c4 to submit recorder-service job 0x1334 with callback 0x00dd4474. That callback maps event 0x114 to message 0x1351, but event 0x103 to message 0x1354. Message 0x1354 selects machine-0x14 state-2 cell 0x00e3f8e8, action 0x00e1557c, transition byte 0xfd, which the dispatcher applies as state 3. Source producers of event 0x103 include 0x00e71a54 and 0x00e7d6f0; recorder-service action 0x94 reaches the latter through 0x00e7e2ec when 0x00e74954 permits it. Channel-2 IRQ admission is separately controlled by 0x00663040: after storing its busy flag and callback, it calls registrar 0x0064e918 and returns 0xffffff01 on registrar failure, otherwise enabling +0x354 bit 28 through 0x00664760 unless 0x0089f6e0 inhibits channel 2. The callback pointer and busy flag alone do not prove successful IRQ registration or enablement.
scope: Static X-M1 1.50 contact/event, matrix/action and completion-producer bindings, interpreted alongside the separately emulated snapshots in E-FUJIMOD-XM1-S2-SENSOR-OBSERVATION-150. No host firmware-state seeding or sibling-camera behavior is used.
limitations: The physical timing and required duration/ordering of real contact holds are not established by these source tables.
The recorder-service action-0x94/device producer and alternate event-0x103 producers remain an explicit source-closure dependency; no sensor/RAW callback is assumed to produce message 0x1354.

C decompiler renderings can omit return values and call arguments. The selected matrix bytes and the constant-return action are checked against the image-5 bytes/A32 disassembly; the remaining call chains are source inspection, not execution evidence.
The absent traced channel-2 enable store does not identify a registrar failure or gate value at registration. Actual register state, interrupt production and DMA destination bytes remain unknown.

limitations: Pointers are traced only from MOVT and PC-relative literal constants and aligned image words; MOV/MVN/ORR or rotated immediates, arithmetic construction and RAM-loaded pointers are not traced.
Initial state/event array contents remain an obligation; initializer and reference-consumer proofs are separate and unreviewed for the checker.

label: emulated
claim: Stock X-M1 1.50 with f7-1.nand and synthetic 5120x3348 RAW16 ramp12 document a37ae260 fresh-boots on FujiMod SDK q32j8dja, ram-push 4ba2df90. A modeled Half/Full/Half/Released sequence advances 8M/8M/4M/4M instructions with one S1 IRQ and one S2 IRQ, followed by exactly one 40M observation window. At 877360000 aggregate instructions boundary.failure is null. After the sequence, read-only image-input state selects channel-2 destination 0x15c12230, left 0, top 60, width 4968, height 3288, packed12 format 3, row bytes 7452 and pitch 7680. Six 48-byte RAM segments decode 192 pixels matching the synthetic ramp, with zero mismatches; the same segments match after the observation window. Device capture_ack changes from false before the sequence to true afterward. Pre-sequence destination bytes were not sampled because the sampler does not support channel-2 format 0. RAW open and IRQ registration both return zero, while firmware inhibition byte 0x0089f6e0 is 1 at the open branch and remains 1. The actual device register +0x354 is 0x00300000, with IRQ-enable bit28 clear; capture_irq_sent is false. Neither line36/37/38 handlers nor callback 0x00ed84cc execute, and channel-2 enable call/store sites have zero hits. Recorder machines 0x14/0x12/0x4e remain states 2/0/9; action0x94 and callback event0x103 are not observed. No codec/save chain, accepted SD write or new JPEG is observed. The existing JPEG and original/copied card images retain their hashes. Both PNGs show PROGRAM AE help overlays with different dial selections; the final PNG request returns 'no display plane to capture'. UI0x816 is posted during Half before Full. The wrapper exits3 at the card-written gate; bridge ExitSuccess and the command error are retained.
scope: One host-only physical-contact diagnostic on the frozen SDK, using the shared emulator slot, CPUs4-5, CPUQuota25%, MemoryMax4GiB and swap0. This records after-sequence destination samples and device acknowledgement, not a complete frame, physical-camera behavior, still-capture completion or #124/#129/#131 acceptance.
limitations: Pre-sequence destination bytes are unknown. Matching later samples and the capture_ack transition do not isolate the shutter sequence as their cause.
Only six 48-byte segments are checked; whole-frame integrity is unknown.

S is SP at the BL. Premise X: no exception or other agent changes registers, SP or the named memory during the callee, and every load and store completes. Premise F: memory is flat and non-aliasing. Every interval, disjointness and 'no store at or above' statement here is over numeric addresses and implies distinct storage only under F. X-M1 has guest aliases (at least 0 and 0x40000000), so numerically distinct addresses may name one location, for example a frame at 0x414fee08 against a store at 0x014fee08. It pushes r4 and r11 to [S-8,S), sets r11=S-4 and does not write r11 again, so it returns with SP=S whatever memory holds. With its instruction bytes intact, for n=0 it stores nothing and for n>0 it makes exactly n byte stores, in order, at dst+k mod 2^32 for k<n. Byte k stored is the byte loaded at src+k at that moment for k<m and 0 for m<=k<n, with m the first k<n whose loaded byte is 0 (else n). It loads only src+0..src+min(m,n-1). Those are the entry-time source bytes if the source span is disjoint from the destination span and from [S-8,S), neither span wraps 2^32 and the destination span misses [0x00721b40,0x00721bac); none of this is shown for general pointers. It writes r1, r2 (0 at return), r3 and r12, leaves r0, r5-r10 and lr unchanged, and returns r4 and r11 as the words at [S-8,S) after its stores. F1 writes no SP from 0x01239dfc to 0x01239e58 and under X each call returns SP=S, so S is the same at all three. Inductively under X and F: [S-8,S) disjoint from W1 keeps r4 and r11 across the first call, so the second stores W2; disjoint from W2 keeps them across the second, so the third stores W3; disjoint from W3 keeps them at 0x01239e38. On these two paths under X and F it returns with SP=S, r4-r10 unchanged and no store at or above S, so the caller's pushed r3, r4, r11 and lr words survive. (4) The remaining path calls 0x0071f418(i, r1). It pops r3, r4, r11 and pc by SP and, when word[0x00917f64+4*i]=0, calls 0x00701ce4(i) and so 0x007065b8(i), whose 18 word stores have effective addresses 0x00918848+112*i plus offsets covering every word residue mod 16. claim: The host checker //replacement/modal_runtime:modal-closure at source 46e0251 (binary sha256 98ee62bf913958d45b89678e1335791c3df184cfa6290d589e5c76f229a1256b) attaches a return-continuation witness to each return-conditional stream consumer. Its scope is the code that reaches the materialization by fallthrough and by B edges whose sites lie between the nearest frame prologue at or below it and the materialization. It enumerates A32 B/BL, aligned-word, MOVW/MOVT-pair, PC-relative ADD/SUB and Thumb BL/BLX references into that scope under the address & 0x3fffffff alias classes, and follows each BL caller's continuation, conditionals taken both ways, to its first read or write of the returned register. A call, SVC, return, indirect jump, unmodeled instruction, leaving the images or a cycle with the register live leaves a path unresolved; an alias-only branch, a B from outside the scope, an unreferenced scope start or fallthrough into the start is a non-call entry; a return through lr after an lr write in the scope is a limit. Any of these prevents narrowing. Over the five pinned X-M1 1.50 RAM-push images, the only return-conditional consumer, the plain MOVT 0x012369e8 (0x007b7000 in stream B, returned in r3 at 0x01236a2c), has scope [0x0123696c,0x01236998] and [0x012369d4,0x012369e8] from the push at 0x0123696c, no non-call entry and no limit. Its sole caller BL 0x011f4fec continues at 0x011f4ff0 and writes r3 at 0x011f4ff8 and 0x011f5010 before any read on every path. Its premise therefore narrows to direct-continuations-overwrite with residual premises no-unenumerated-entry, saved-return-slot-integrity, no-asynchronous-write and code-integrity, and it stays return-conditional. Obligations (6,904), controllers, consumer statuses and the per-stream counts (A 39 open, B 1 return-conditional and 70 open, C 127 open) equal closure-inventory-8.json.
limitations: Not a discharge: the consumer stays return-conditional, and the four residual premises are unproved.
Entries are limited to the enumerated reference forms; computed, register-built, exception and other-agent entries are covered only by the no-unenumerated-entry premise.

No frame or data-write disjointness is checked: whether the saved return slots of 0x0123696c and its callees survive the writes into [0x014fe898,0x014fe954) stays the saved-return-slot-integrity premise.
The scope start is the nearest frame prologue found by the existing two-form predicate within 1024 words; it bounds which B edges count as inside, not which references are enumerated.
Only the five pinned images and the linked bank ELF sections are scanned; other kernel and package regions are not.

label: static-inference
claim: The X-M1 1.50 kernel timer at 0xfff91000 counts up in its running mode 0x23, and the stock timer and interrupt-controller laws are recorded register by register in reports/xm1-timer-interrupt-laws.md (static-inference over byte-read instructions and two hardware-observed console stores; host-only). Direction: in the read-log captures 20261009T064945Z and 20261008T024241Z the record field [0xfff91004]-[0xfff91000] falls in all 942 and 3062 same-tick adjacent pairs and rises in none, with every value in 1..29924, so with 0xfff91004 holding the written reload 30000 the counter rises through each tick; the µs busy-wait 0x723ffc (59 call sites) and record 2 channel delay 0x270c are written for a rising counter, while loader 0x41ad4 and the log writers therefore record time remaining in the tick. Pinned FujiMod 3d90035d timer.rs counts mode 0x23 down, which mirrors emulated sub-tick values and shortens 0x723ffc to about one counter step. Rate: 30000 counts per kernel tick at the hardware-observed 99.88 Hz, about 2.996 MHz; boot mode 0x63 (count/1875 per 10 ms), 0x23, 0x53 (375 per unit) and 10,000,000/reload fit one clock divided by 2^((control>>4)&7). IRQ path: loaders A 0x40204 and B 0xd0204 share spin lock 0x400c0804 (17 or 18 by CP14 identity), held from entry to the outermost exit, so stock IRQ handlers are serialized across both cores; handlers run with CPSR.I clear; acknowledge reads bank +0x200 and +0x230, EOI clears pending through +0x120 then writes 0 to +0x200; enable/disable use +0x80/+0xa0/+0x60/+0x100/+0x140/+0x180/+0x400/+0x800/+0xe0/+0x120 on the bank selected by CP14 identity 0x4003 (0xfffb3000) or other (0xfffb4000); line 32 (tick, priority 1) is enabled by both loaders on their own bank and line 120 (priority 0) is the cross-core reschedule line pended through +0xc0 by notifiers A 0x44018 and B 0xd3fd4. Periodic callbacks such as 0x72337c targets run from the tick IRQ with IRQ unmasked under that lock.
scope: Gate 1 of #156: device-law inventory for an embassy time driver and interrupt glue. Host-only; no guest or camera run. Hardware evidence is two earlier read-log captures; physical controller arbitration, priority sense, enable-register semantics, mode fields, counter range and reload latch timing remain unknowns U1-U13 with experiment designs.
limitations: The direction conclusion assumes 0xfff91004 reads back the written reload 30000 (U1); only the difference is hardware-observed.
Slot order is taken as write order; read-log windows are not an atomic snapshot, and pairs break at zero slots and the next index.
The 2.996 MHz figure assumes one line-32 IRQ per 30000-count period; the 12 MHz input clock is [INFERENCE] from firmware constants.

Controller arbitration, priority sense, nesting gating, +0x80 write semantics, +0xe0 versus +0x120, mode fields, +0x40, +0x1c0/+0x1c4/+0x1c8/+0xc00, software pend of lines other than 120, WFI wake with CPSR.I set and line-32 fan-out are not grounded on hardware.

claim: The first 256-byte windows of the 0x400a0800 syslog store read in sessions 20261008T020826Z-read-log and 20261008T024241Z-read-log on XM1-body-01 (official 1.50, maintenance mode) differ in 23 bytes, and nothing yet explains the difference. Apart from the header's next-index halfword at +0x1e, every type-0x09 slot (slots 0-3, from +0x34) and the header copy at +0x24 differ at arg1 (+2) and at the delta (+0xc): slot 0 holds arg1 0x68 and delta 0x74b2 in the first read and arg1 0x67 and delta 0x74b3 in the second, and the arg1 values of slots 0-3 read 0x68, 0x67, 0x66, 0x5d in the first and 0x67, 0x68, 0x5d, 0x66 in the second. Every type-0x0f slot in the window differs in its +2 delta halfword. The tick fields are equal. The two sessions were recorded as one maintenance boot, and the header index moved from 4050 to 4055 between them. Two explanations fit: a reboot between the sessions, after which loader A's initializer rewrote the store with the same early records (E-LOG-PERSIST-150), or a rewrite of the early slots within one boot.

scope: X-M1 1.50 stock no-card cold boot to SHOOTING MENU (1,5,2) on the pinned FujiMod 3d90035d default model (timer up-count, boot-ROM decode, core-1 identity 0x8003) through //emulation:fujimod-flash-boot-check with the opt-in power-hold log; one independently reviewed observer run; the writer identity is also byte-read from boot record 1.
claim: On the stock cold boot every access to the power-hold word 0xfff88084 is four core-0 accesses, all before 80,000,000 instructions: the ROM init stores 1 (CPU-view PC 0xec = ROM 0x800000ec, tick 2, board instruction 51), the configuration apply stores 0 (PC 0x330, tick 193, instruction 4,637), and boot record 1 reads 0 at listing offset 0x26ec and stores 1 at 0x26f4 (tick 2,676). No further access occurs through the menu at 383,750,000 instructions; core 1 never touches the word. Under the clock model (exr2/clock.rs: a bit-0-clear write arms a 100,000-tick supply-off deadline when none is pending, a bit-0-set write cancels it) the deadline arms once at tick 193, due 100,193, and is cancelled 2,483 ticks later; the model's own hold state equals this replay at all 25 stops and reads held with no deadline from the boot stop on. Byte-read: boot-40048 0x26e8-0x26f4 is mvn r3,#0x77000 (0xfff88fff); ldr r2,[r3,#-0xf7b]; orr r2,r2,#1; str r2,[r3,#-0xf7b], inside the routine that also programs the kernel timer 0xfff91000. The address is formed without any 0xfff88000-0xfff880ff constant, which is why the earlier reference scan missed it; this corrects the no-later-writer clause of E-SDBOOT-NOTE-HOLD-BINDING-150 for boot record 1. The model's supply-off law is therefore consistent with the camera staying on, and no model fix is proposed.

label: static-inference
claim: Declared assumption, not hardware fact: the default FujiMod stack now ends a four-byte byte-mode DMA CMD53 to function 1 (0x353a0001 write, 0x353a0011 read, block size 4, block count 0) to the enumeration-protocol Wi-Fi module with a host command timeout (error status 0x32 bit 0, normal status 0x30 bit 15), zero response and no data; block, PIO and other CMD53 forms still stop the machine. The X-M1 1.50 driver (static reading of the plain image): opening PC AUTO SAVE SETTING > SIMPLE SETUP, menu (83,177), reaches WLAN_Start 0x013e40cc, probe 0x012af3ac and module reset 0x01292024, whose first CMD53 at 0x0129216c writes 0x8000 to function 1 register 0x8c (argument 0x90011804, DMA buffer 0x014760c0). The wait 0x0128fb48 polls 0x30/0x32 directly and leaves when 0x32 & 0x17ff is nonzero; 0x012918e8/0x01291884 replace every CMD53 failure with success. The reset then polls a CMD53 read of 0x8c for bit 0x800 up to 512 times with sleeps and returns 0xC0000001, the probe fails and WLAN_Start returns -255 through an empty logging stub, without retry. A command timeout is the outcome that asserts nothing about the module; under the firmware mask every failure form gives the same driver result.
scope: FujiMod SDIO host model under the X-M1 run document and its host checks; no guest run under the change.
limitations: No X-M1 capture records the Wi-Fi module answers, its CCCR or CIS, its register map or whether it needs a firmware download; whether the real module answers this CMD53 is unknown.
The X-M1 driver reading is static (plain.dis); its classifier 0x0129026c returns 5 or 7 only when the polling-mode shadow 0x0146b874 is current, which the CMD53 mask makes immaterial.
What the UI does after WLAN_Start returns -255 was not traced.
The Run-3 camera dump and the FujiMod calibration dump hold WLAN driver state byte 0x014be62c = 0 at the shooting screen; neither covers SIMPLE SETUP.
The property-pair route that stopped on this command has not been rerun under the change.
Module identity is unresolved: the service manual names DWM-W094 and the FCC filing photo shows another part.

label: source-inspected
scope: Host diagnosis of two preserved guarded picker receipts and static reading of loader kernel code in the Run-3 RAM dump; host tests only, no guest run under the fixed guard.
claim: The lifetime guard refused a legitimate cross-core race. Loader A dispatch loads the selected cell 0x40054768 at 0x436b0 and stores it to current at 0x436b8 with IRQ masked and no lock; make-ready on core 1 (0xd3c60, selected-cell store 0xd3cc4) can write that cell for a primary task in between. In picker-15-stock and picker-211-owned (ControllerStrategy picker-runs-2) the last core-0 rows are its context save before 0x436b8, core 1 then runs make-ready on primary node 42, and the stop count equals core 0's count at 0x436b4 plus 1000; no other context site is reachable there. The guard compared r1 with the selected cell read at prepare time and refused with invalid_context. Cross-core make-ready of primary nodes appears in every pre-merge and post-merge receipt examined, so the merge's model changes shifted timing rather than adding the path. Fix: both selected cells are write-watched; a value the other core's make-ready replaced stays admissible for the kernel's next current-task store until that store or its own core's next write to the cell (at most 17: 16 ready-queue levels and null); unexplained mismatches still refuse.
limitations: The selected cell was not watched in the failing runs, so the write that changed it is inferred from make-ready's code and the recorded node writes; kernel B ready-queue removal stores (0xd3d5c, 0xd3d78) are not excluded and remain refused.
The 1000-instruction slice is inferred from the counts.
No guarded rerun under the fixed guard has run.

compareKernelCase compares the multiset of writes with their values, not their order; final values come from the writable and device regions, and barrier order is left to per-case assertions on the ordered log.
The FujiMod exclusive monitor across cores, the stock-run PC watches and the shared layout crate of design step S0 are not covered here.

The mask smoke establishes architectural I/F-bit execution only; it does not model interrupt delivery, task scheduling, full native coverage or hardware timing. Completed proofs remain bound to their original runner identities.
Optional contexts track a bounded voluntary fixed-mode ABI only. IRQ/preemption, SPSR exception return, mode-changing continuations and complete task lifecycle are not qualified.
Context declarations never supply guest frames, task records or saved SP/PC. The RTOS family must qualify its own real state, effect and lifetime predicates with disjoint synthetic fixture stacks.
The continuation proof does not transfer the partial RTOS family results, full native coverage, an integrated subsystem comparison or hardware evidence to the new runner.

The single-pop admission is the exact standard e49df004 form under existing condition/profile checks. Other loaded-PC forms retain their existing restrictions. No broader control-flow or memory-permission relaxation is established.
